summary: Master and stage branches diff script
description:
As a Keycloak Developer I want a script that can verify whether the stage branch is identical to the master branch (after the merging process). Using {{git diff}} is advised.
Acceptance criteria:
* The script takes one argument: the repository identifier (e.g. {{keycloak/keycloak}})
* Exit code equals 0 if the branches are identical.
* Non-zero exit code is used otherwise.

summary: Test matrix of JVM and operating systems
description:
This JIRA is about running the Keycloak testsuite on auth-server-wildfly/auth-server-eap on various OS and with various Java versions on each OS.
The first step is to clarify what are the required needed combinations to test with.
Regarding testing on RHEL, then based on this page in the section "Tested Configurations: Red Hat Single Sign-On 7.3", it seems that we need to test with rhel6, rhel7 and rhel8. Regarding java versions, there is "Oracle JDK 1.8, 11, IBM JDK 1.8, Red Hat OpenJDK 1.8, 11 " . So I think that we may need to test with all those combinations in the pipeline too. I've created the subtask KEYCLOAK-10500 for this. Regarding the existing matrix job on jenkins, I can see this one . See the configuration of the job and what/how to trigger tests. Also see the adapter pipeline for an inspiration on how to test specific combinations and an example how to skip testing of some combinations - .
Once we have all the "rhel" tests in pipeline and stable, the other step is testing on windows. Created subtask KEYCLOAK-10501 for this. See the jenkins job for this .

summary: Pass All Conformance Tests for FAPI OpenID testsuite after Keycloak 15
description:
Part of this task is to:
- Make sure that Keycloak master (currently still before KEycloak 15 release) is able to pass the FAPI conformance testsuite . We go for the server tests (OP) for the FAPI. We may possibly obtain the certifications for all the configurations from:

-- Brazil Open Banking (Based on FAPI 1 Advanced Final) from - We should be able to obtain certifications for first 8 configurations. For the 9th (DCR), there may be some customizations needed on Keycloak side to receive the certification
-- FAPI CIBA from . Possibly all 4 configurations.
- After Keycloak 15 release, obtain the certifications
- Acknowledge the FAPI, FAPI CIBA and OpenBanking Brasil certifications obtained (documentation? Blogpost? Something else?)

summary: Create independent message bundle
description:
Right now, the New Account Console relies on the old message bundle. This bundle does not contain all the needed messages and we really shouldn't be adding to the old bundle that the old account console uses.
So we need to create an independent message bundle for the new account console. As part of this task we need to make sure that there are no hard-coded strings in the new account console.

summary: Improve support for setting keys for OIDC clients
description:
This is follow-up on adding encrypted ID Tokens support - KEYCLOAK-6768 .
In recent Keycloak version, we have support for Encrypted OIDC ID Tokens. It will be good to add better support to admin console to be able to specify the client's public key, which will be used to encrypt the assertion, so that client can decrypt the particular assertion with it's private key. The only way to do this is to specify JWKS URL of the client, but to enable it, you need to configure client credentials of type "Signed JWT" even if you don't want this credential to authenticate client. And there is no way to hardcode the public key for token's encryption at this moment. So to better support we may need to:
- Introduce new tab "OIDC Keys" or "Keys" to the OIDC clients. If we introduce tab "Keys", we may need to rename tab "SAML Keys" for SAML client, to have OIDC and SAML clients consistent.
- This new tab will allow to have switch "Use JWKS URL". If switch is ON, it will allow to configure JWKS URL. If switch is OFF, there will be a possibility to hardcode (manually configure) client keys used for SIG and ENC similarly like it is currently in the "Credentials -> Signed JWT".
- In the tab "Credentials -> Signed JWT", there will be just info that you need to configure JWKS URL or Signing key in the tab "Keys" - so no 
configuration options on this page. Similarly the tooltips for the options for encrypted ID Token support will contain the tooltip, that you should configure JWKS URL or "hardcode" encryption key in the tab "Keys" .
See the mailing list discussion for the details:

summary: [SPIKE] Best practices for concurrency control in the REST API
description:
When designing REST API, one of the most prominent challenge is concurrency control. The easiest approach is last change which implies in ignoring any change that might have taken place between reading and updating the record. 
In this SPIKE we expect to have a conclusion about which approach is the best for us: optimistic or pessimistic concurrency control.

We should somehow limit what is downloaded to what is only necessary for the page user opens.

description:
First version of W3C Web Authentication support ( KEYCLOAK-9360 ) doesn't have support for attestation statement verification.
This JIRA will require:
- Adding options "Indirect" and "Direct" to Attestation Conveyance Preference in the WebAuthn policy.
- Ensure that proper webauthn4j functions are called based on the requested attestation conveyance preference
- Introducing of apache-kerby-asn1 library as a Wildfly module may be needed for verify android and TPM attestation statements (which will require that RH is able to productize it, so may require some other subtask related to that).
- Ability to obtain trust anchors.
[~tnorimat] mentioned in the design document 
{code}
In order to verify Attestation Statement, keycloak needs to get its trust anchor's certificate. It is plausible to get the trust anchor's certificate in the following ways :
- obtained from FIDO Alliance Metadata Services.
- obtained from an authenticator's vendor.
{code}
Not sure it makes sense, but we can check if we can use the existing TrustStore SPI available in Keycloak. The SPI allows to have set of known trusted certificates. For performance (or other) purpose, it can be beneficial if the certificate of authenticator's vendor is added manually to the truststore file used by Keycloak and hence will be always available without a need to somehow obtain it from the authenticator. That's to be investigated whether this is valid option or not...
When this feature is to be supported, it is needed to consider the above two ways to get the trust anchors' certificates.
full_text:
Support for attestation statement verification

First version of W3C Web Authentication support ( KEYCLOAK-9360 ) doesn't have support for attestation statement verification.
This JIRA will require:
- Adding options "Indirect" and "Direct" to Attestation Conveyance Preference in the WebAuthn policy.
- Ensure that proper webauthn4j functions are called based on the requested attestation conveyance preference
- Introducing of apache-kerby-asn1 library as a Wildfly module may be needed for verify android and TPM attestation statements (which will require that RH is able to productize it, so may require some other subtask related to that).
- Ability to obtain trust anchors.
[~tnorimat] mentioned in the design document 
{code}
In order to verify Attestation Statement, keycloak needs to get its trust anchor's certificate. It is plausible to get the trust anchor's certificate in the following ways :
- obtained from FIDO Alliance Metadata Services.
- obtained from an authenticator's vendor.
{code}
Not sure it makes sense, but we can check if we can use the existing TrustStore SPI available in Keycloak. The SPI allows to have set of known trusted certificates. For performance (or other) purpose, it can be beneficial if the certificate of authenticator's vendor is added manually to the truststore file used by Keycloak and hence will be always available without a need to somehow obtain it from the authenticator. That's to be investigated whether this is valid option or not...
When this feature is to be supported, it is needed to consider the above two ways to get the trust anchors' certificates.

kcinit and it's associated text-based authentication flows adds quite a bit of complexity. It was never fully completed and we don't have capacity to complete it.

* Tests - I think they even checkout and build the kcinit go library

* KeycloakInstalled needs to be reverted
There may be other things also affected by kcinit.

summary: Investigate chrome testing API
description:
It seems that Chrome Testing API is one possibility how to test WebAuthn. The advantage is, that it is relatively close to the real environment as JS calls "navigator.credentials.create()" and "navigatore.credentials.get()" are performed. 
Disadvantages are, that it doesn't allow to test all WebAuthn features, it requires particular version of Chrome and WebDriver (hence doesn't work everywhere) and Chrome headless mode doesn't work.
We need to doublecheck if it's possible to run the tests on jenkins. This will mean that we can use it to test at least some parts of WebAuthn integration with it.

summary: Using fine-grained admin permissions on groups, users should be able to create users without the role 'manage-users' according to the group permissions
description:
Using fine-grained admin permissions on groups, a user in a group with *scope* permission 'manage' role should be able to create new users without the role 'manage-users'.
We have a scenario where we need to separate users in particular groups from each other. This works very well using fine-grained admin permissions with 'query-groups' and 'query-users' on realm-management client.
A local_admin_1 could only query users in group "users" and group "local admin", but could not see any super admin like "root admin".
However, the local_admin_1 could not create a user. If we add 'manager-users' to the group roles under realm-management client, all users are visible and no permissions are evaluated.
This is an essential use-case for our projects and is some-how related to #KEYCLOAK-7884
in one of the screenshots it can be seen that the option to create a new user is given, but once the dialog opens, the button "create" is not available.

summary: Implementation of Two-Factor authentication endpoint
description:
h2. What
* As part of [single credentials page| we need to implement the UI and also the endpoint to allow users to set up Two-Factor authentication. To manage 2FA and backup codes they should be requested to re-authenticate using the implementation of [Application Initiated Actions (phase III)|
h2. Why
* Users should be able to protect their accounts by setting up 2-step verification, as they already do today. And also, be able to disable or remove Two-Factor authentication methods and their respective backup codes.
h2. How
* User visits the single credentials page based on the [Feedback document| and is presented with the Two-Factor authentication section as part of it.
{noformat}
Two-Factor Authentication
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[ON|OFF] Two-factor authentication is enabled.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[G]	Mobile Authenticator	(Default)					[...] (Hamburger menu with options like delete/update)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[B]	Backup codes								[...] (Hamburger menu with options like delete/update)
{noformat}
h2. Acceptance Criteria
* User can configure a new 2FA authentication method 
* User can enable/disable Two-Factor authentication
* User can delete or update 2FA method
* User can delete or update method
* *Condition*: For each action above, user should be requested to re-authenticate by providing {{password}} and {{OTP}} if enabled 
h2. Additional Information
* For such implementation {{SMS}} is out of scope

full_text:
Implementation of Two-Factor authentication endpoint

h2. What
* As part of [single credentials page| we need to implement the UI and also the endpoint to allow users to set up Two-Factor authentication. To manage 2FA and backup codes they should be requested to re-authenticate using the implementation of [Application Initiated Actions (phase III)|
h2. Why
* Users should be able to protect their accounts by setting up 2-step verification, as they already do today. And also, be able to disable or remove Two-Factor authentication methods and their respective backup codes.
h2. How
* User visits the single credentials page based on the [Feedback document| and is presented with the Two-Factor authentication section as part of it.
{noformat}
Two-Factor Authentication
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[ON|OFF] Two-factor authentication is enabled.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[G]	Mobile Authenticator	(Default)					[...] (Hamburger menu with options like delete/update)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[B]	Backup codes								[...] (Hamburger menu with options like delete/update)
{noformat}
h2. Acceptance Criteria
* User can configure a new 2FA authentication method 
* User can enable/disable Two-Factor authentication
* User can delete or update 2FA method
* User can delete or update method
* *Condition*: For each action above, user should be requested to re-authenticate by providing {{password}} and {{OTP}} if enabled 
h2. Additional Information
* For such implementation {{SMS}} is out of scope

summary: Reduce startup-time of Keycloak on Quarkus
description:
Keycloak on Quarkus starts in 10-15 seconds, which even though it is faster than Keycloak on WildFly is far from the promise Quarkus delivers (REST+JPA in 2.5 seconds, see 
There is two likely candidates for reducing the startup-time:
* How the EntityManagerFactory is created
* Liquibase
For Liquibase there's two things we can look into:
* Creating a start from scratch schema, which doesn't go through the endless migration of the schema
* Creating native schemas for some dbs at build-time, which may be quicker than Liquibase going through it manually

summary: Back button fix when switching flows
description:
There is a bug in "Back" button history. Scenario:
- Configure browser flow with the usernameForm and PasswordForm instead of default UsernamePasswordForm
- Enable "Forget password" for the realm
- Trigger authentication and fill username on the 1st screen. I will be redirected to Password screen, which contains "Forget password" link.
- Click on the "Forget password". I am redirected to Reset-credentials flow, but I can see "Back" button even if this is 1st screen of reset-password flow -> BUG
- Click on the "Back" button. Now I am redirected to the screen with UsernameForm and execution corrresponds to executionId of the UsernameForm of browser authenticator. But the flow is still reset-password -> BUG
Reason of this behaviour is, that at this moment, the AuthenticationFlowHistoryHelper doesn't consider more top-level flows during same authenticationSession. So when user switch to different flow (EG. from browser to reset-password) he see "Back" button and he can go to the authentication execution from different flow, which is a bug. Maybe the authenticationSession note SUCCESSFUL_ACTION_EXECUTIONS can have a namespace with having the flow name as a prefix in the name of the note? That will allow to track history of more flows in same authentication session.

description:
There's a useful behaviour of the back button which has been lost with the latest changes, the ability to return to a previous sub-flow when there's a selection of alternative executions, with one of the executions being a subflow.
In the attached image, you can select between webauthn and password with second factor. In the previous behaviour, you could select the "password with 2nd" factor flow to go to the password form, and use the back button to move back to the selection of the "Authentication" flow, which would basically put you back to the webAuthn form, but now you will move back to the username form, since it's the last successful action.
Possibly the solution is to add the current execution to the SUCCESSFUL_ACTION_EXECUTIONS stack when selecting an alternative flow as an action

summary: WebAuthn: polish after rebase
description:
After rebase prototype with latest Keycloak master, WebAuthn was added to the prototype as it is already available in latest Keycloak master. We may have some remaining things to discuss & clarify. This JIRA is just to handle this possible remaining work around clarifying those points.
In case we agree that there is nothing more needed, we may just close the JIRA :)
The points were discussed on zulip (room #dev-auth and topic "multi-factor rebase"), so just copy/paste it here:
1) I've added the WebAuthnCredentialModel class (compatible with OTPCredentialModel and PasswordCredentialModel introduced in the prototype) and I've added fields 
"aaguid", "credentialId" and "counter" as part of CredentialData and "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" as part of SecretData. The only reason why I did is, 
that secretData are not displayed in the admin console. See screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-39-46.png
I am not sure if displaying "AttestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" won't make the data too big. But strictly said, WebAuthn credential doesn't have any confidential data. So should be "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" added to CredentialData too and displayed in the admin console? This will mean secretData will be just empty. WDYT?
2) The WebAuthn works in a bit different way than OTP. The WebAuthn authentication javascript call to "navigator.credentials.get" allows to pass more IDs of webAuthn credentials to the list of "allowed-credentials" and client itself can decide which credential he wants to use. So regarding this, I see few options:
a) The WebAuthnAuthenticator won't inherit from CredentialValidator interface. This means that in the Credentials selector list, which is described here there will be just single label "WebAuthn" . When this label is chosen, the checkbox is displayed when user can select the WebAuthn credentials, which he wants to use. This is the approach, which I used so far and you can see the screenshot how it looks like the screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-15-49.png
b) The WebAuthnAuthenticator will inherit from CredentialValidator interface. So Credentials selector list will contain separate items for each credential with labels like "WebAuthn - yubikey", "WebAuthn - chrome test" . There won't be checkbox selection on the page. So WebAuthn call to "navigator.credentials.get" will be always called just with single allowed credential.
c) Hybrid of 2 options above. There will be 2 labels and when particular label is chosen, the checkbox selection will be displayed as well on the WebAuthn page, but just with the single credential selected by default, which will correspond to the selected label. User has ability to select more credentials if he wants.
3) I removed the attributes from UserModel as I mentioned. Regarding the credentialId, I kept it just as single item in the WebAuthnCredentialData. In the keycloak master, you had it saved defacto 2 times:
a) the user attribute, which corresponds to the Base64URL encoded "rawId" returned from navigator.credentials.create
b) The attribute on the credential, which corresponds to the Base64 encoded of AttestedCredentialData.getCredentialId .
It seems to me from the WebAuthn specification and from my testing with yubikey and chrome testing api, that both those "credentialsId" are defacto same. So is it ok to save it just once in the credential model? In other words, the item returned from "rawId" is not saved.

summary: OpenID Connect Financial-grade API: Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication Profile
description:
Add the ability to add an authentication flow where the actual the user provides authentication credentials in a separate channel.
Like Google Push Authenticator, the IDP sends a push message that encodes a transaction, the app receives the push msg, decodes, and prompts the user to confirm (which signs the transaction). This signature is then sent to the IDP and thus allows access to the user in the original triggering channel. The only thing the user has to supply original triggering channel is a user identifier, no credentials.
There are two two related standards for this
* (Old & depericated) OIDC Modrna CIBA @
* (New) OIDC Modrna FAPI CIBA @
** This also has the Logding Intent mechanism to allow transaction data (that is to be signed by the user mobile device) to be sent via the back channel and the returned scope_id can then be sent via the standard OIDC mechanims.

summary: Identity Brokering Sync Mode
description:
h2. What?
Add a sync mode option to identity providers that controls how the user profile is updated.
h2. Why?
Identity providers have different use-cases, which requires user profiles to be synced differently. In essence this can be summarised to the following use-cases:
* Registration/authentication - users register through an external identity provider (often a social network). The account is then managed fully within Keycloak afterwards.
* External users - a group of external users is able to login to Keycloak to access applications secured with Keycloak, but users are fully managed in the external identity provider
* Hybrid - users can be managed both externally and internally
The above use-cases are conflicting to each other. For example if the users first name is always updated when the user authenticates through the external identity provider it will work fine in the external users use-case, but in the first use-case the user updates the first name in Keycloak account console, but can then be reverted next time the user logs in.
h2. How?
Add a "sync-mode" option to identity providers. Sync-mode should have the following options:
* legacy - keep the current behaviour
* import - user profiles are only updated on import/registration, and will not be updated on subsequent logins
* owner - user profile will be updated on subsequent logins if the user has a single identity link and has not been modified directly in Keycloak
* force - always update the user profile
Further, to allow flexibility individual mappers should have a sync-mode option as well. By default it will not be set, which will use the sync-mode of the identity provider, but it can be directly set on individual mappers to override the behaviour for a specific mapper.
All identity provider mappers need to be updated to support sync-mode.

summary: Make sure admin can't break access
description:
At the moment there are several things that an admin could do that would break access to the server completely. For example:
* Disable master realm
* Delete internal clients/roles
* Change to a broken custom authentication flow
We need to either make sure this can't happen, or that there is a way to revert/restore access.
full_text:
Make sure admin can't break access

At the moment there are several things that an admin could do that would break access to the server completely. For example:
* Disable master realm
* Delete internal clients/roles
* Change to a broken custom authentication flow
We need to either make sure this can't happen, or that there is a way to revert/restore access.

summary: User should be evicted from cache when their credential is deleted
description:
In admin console:
1. Create a test user
2. Go to the credentials page of the test user
3. Set password credential for the test user
4. Delete the created password credential
5. Attempt to log in as the test user with the deleted password
Expected result: Login fails.
Actual result: Login is successful, until user is evicted from the cache.
full_text:
User should be evicted from cache when their credential is deleted

In admin console:
1. Create a test user
2. Go to the credentials page of the test user
3. Set password credential for the test user
4. Delete the created password credential
5. Attempt to log in as the test user with the deleted password
Expected result: Login fails.
Actual result: Login is successful, until user is evicted from the cache.

summary: Unable to save newly created password credentials
description:
In admin console:
1. Create a test user
2. Go to the credentials page of the test user
3. Set password credential for the test user
4. Click the "Save" button for the password credential
Expected result: Credential is saved.
Actual result: 
UI shows: "Error while updating the credential. See console for more information."
Request to "{{.../auth/admin/realms/test/users/.../credentials/.../label}}" returns: "415 Unsupported Media Type". The {{Content-Type}} header is missing from the request.
Workaround: Set any value in the User Label field, and click "Save". This will add {{Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8}} to the next request.
full_text:
Unable to save newly created password credentials

In admin console:
1. Create a test user
2. Go to the credentials page of the test user
3. Set password credential for the test user
4. Click the "Save" button for the password credential
Expected result: Credential is saved.
Actual result: 
UI shows: "Error while updating the credential. See console for more information."
Request to "{{.../auth/admin/realms/test/users/.../credentials/.../label}}" returns: "415 Unsupported Media Type". The {{Content-Type}} header is missing from the request.
Workaround: Set any value in the User Label field, and click "Save". This will add {{Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8}} to the next request.

summary: Usability - Rename all ConditionalBlockAuthenticator to ConditionalAuthenticator
description:
We have some feedback from the Keycloak team regarding usability of new authentication flows. One of the points was to change some labels. For example change the "Conditional block - user configured" to the "Condition - user configured" . In relation to that we can possibly rename all the classes in "conditional" package and remove the work "Block" from them? Like for example ConditionalBlockAuthenticatorFactory to ConditionalAuthenticatorFactory etc. WDYT? If you are fine with that and we have time, we can maybe even manage to do this for Keycloak 8 (current prototype).
Note that these changes will require going over the additions in the documentation to change the name in the text and in the screenshots.

summary: Discuss: reset-credentials flow and ability to reset single credential
description:
Assume following setup:
- Default reset-credentials flow (which has ResetOTP authenticator as conditional)
- User john has TOTP setup on his account
- User john wants to login and he clicks "Forget password" during login
- Right now, he is required to setup his password, but also OTP. This is bit strange as he clicked on "Forget password", so why he is required to reset his OTP too? Similarly it may not be obvious to him, that reset of his OTP is possible by click to "Forget password" link.
It will be probably better to:
- Have a way to reset/setup each credential separately. So when user clicks on "Forget password" on password form, he will reset just his password. When he clicks on "Forget OTP" on OTP form, he will reset just his OTP.
This may require some changes in the reset-credentials flow - maybe remove authenticators ResetPassword and ResetOTP entirely from the flow. And when user successfully "authenticates" with this flow (which by default means that he does email verification), he will be allowed to reset single credential.
We can check if it makes sense to use AIA for this flow.

summary: Discuss: Adding WebAuthn Register required action by default to the realm?

Whether to do this or not, may depend if WebAuthn will be technology preview (enabled by default with custom profile) .

summary: Set password VS Reset Password
description:
When admin wants to reset password of the keycloak user in credentials tab, then:
- In latest keycloak master (before authentication prototype is added), there is always button "Reset password" allowing admin to reset user's password
- In the prototype, this is changed that there is button "Set password" instead of reset password. And when the user already has password set, this option is not available. So to reset password, admin needs to remove password credential from the user and then he can "Set password" .
Question is, whether to have the same behaviour as was before the prototype (Reset password) or keep current behaviour.
In both cases, admin console tests may need to be changed/fixed.

summary: Apply password history policy when password reset by admin?
description:
It seems that the password history policy isn't applied when the password credential is deleted and re-created in the admin console. It's only being applied in the user's account management console when user tries to reset the password.
IMO this is behaviour is fine, but that's for the discussion... The admin console test "PasswordPolicyTest.testPasswordHistoryPolicy()" is currently failing/ignored because of that.

summary: Ensure that REQUIRED and ALTERNATIVE executions are not mixed at same level
description:
It will be nice to make sure that REQUIRED and ALTERNATIVE executions are not mixed at same level (same authentication subflow). AFAIK when this is currently configured, it causes that ALTERNATIVE executions are just ignored. This could be confusing as it may not be obvious to admin, that ALTERNATIVE execution is ignored in this case.
So will be nice to make sure that it is not possible to configure authentication flow this way. If it is already configured (which can be possible during migrations from same level), then make sure that ALTERNATIVE executions are somehow hidden or clearly marked in the UI, so that it's obvious, that they are defacto ignored.

summary: Possible bug during export/import of required actions
Polish the layout of alerts
description:
The alerts justs "look weird". I can see at least two or three clear issues with them.
# The message is not centered, it's closer to the bottom of the alert. This is probably caused by the alert title which is present but empty (and therefore not visible) but takes place anyway.
# The alerts are placed in the page "heading box". You can see in the attached screenshot that the box above Personal Info heading is stretched. The alert should probably be placed *above* the "heading box", not inside it.
# We might also want to reconsider how the alerts are displayed. Currently, the alert is placed above the main content pushing it down. But when the alert is closed (either manually or automatically after a few seconds), the main content "jumps up". Let's imagine a user is about to click some button in the main content, moves the mouse cursor, but then then the content together with the button "jumps" because an alert was automatically closed. We should either display the alert as a "floating" box temporarily overlapping the content, or "reserve" a small space for the alerts above the main content which would be empty when no alert is displayed.
# Some animation would be nice when displaying and closing an alert. Currently it looks a bit clumsy.

summary: Re-evaluate usage of UserStorage providers
description:
I think that before the prototype was done, it was possible to delegate verification of OTP (and other) credentials to 3rd party UserStorage provider in case that particular UserStorage provider had support for OTP credential.
This surely still works for passwords as LDAP provider provides password validation.
This JIRA exists just to doublecheck if there is no regression of this capability with respect of OTP (and other) credential types. In other words, if admin implemented 3rd party UserStorage provider, which provides validation/update of TOTP, then doublecheck that it will still work. I have some small doubts as OTPFormAuthenticator now directly calls "getCredentialProvider().isValid()" instead of "session.userCredentialManager().isValid()" as was before.

Currently, even with the [KEYCLOAK-11745 MFA prototype change included| if the parent flow is disabled, the child subflows are still editable / configurable. Since this is misleading (might cause confusion), we should consider implementing a change, that would hide the subflows, if the parent flow is disabled (or alternatively make them as non-sensitive / non-editable at the very least).

* If the "_*Browser - Conditional OTP*_" flow is "_*DISABLED*_", the:
* "_*Condition - User Configured*_" and
* "_*OTP Form*_"
subflows are still visible, and editable.

summary: "Invalid username or password." message displayed upon entering invalid username in the UsernameForm
description:
As [noticed / reported by| [~vmuzikar] there's {noformat}"Invalid username or password." {noformat} message displayed in the (newly, by KEYCLOAK-11745 change added) _*UsernameForm*_, when the user provides invalid user name.
This should be changed:
# Not to speak about _"password"_ in the message (since no password was provided yet),
# But should use a bit more sophisticated mechanism how to inform the user, that invalid user name was provided than just plain "Invalid username.", since this could be use for valid usernames enumeration brute-force attack, if used in this form. Maybe look how other providers, implementing MFA recognize this use case, and report the state back, without leaking the fact if the user exists or not.

summary: Design proposal for login screen for select 2 factor authenticators
description:
We may want some nice design for the login screens. The ideal candidate to start with could be the page for selecting alternative 2-factor authenticators.
The page might be similar to the slide 12 on those slides - . Few more additional points to clarify:
- This particular example uses password, OTP and WebAuthn as 2nd factor authenticators. In reality, password will likely never be 2nd factor authenticator, but for this example, we can assume that it may be and we may need the icon for it as well.
- The labels will be just "Password", "Authenticator application" and "Security key" . There 
won't be text like "Login with" at the beginning. These texts will be provided by authenticator implementations, no need to care too much about concrete texts in the design
- There will be some nice icon at the beginning for each authentication mechanism. Each authenticator will be able to provide CSS class of it's own.
- Ideal will be if there is arrow at the end of each line, so it is more clear that this is clickable link. Or something like this.
- Lines between items could be nice. Also some nice border for the table maybe...
- We may want to display username/email on this screen as well. As user (or at least his username) will be already known. Username can be displayed above the table. When user clicks on this username, the whole authentication flow should be restarted. It may be nice if it is somehow emphasized that username is clickable and that clicking on it will restart the login. Or alternatively, we can add hover like "Restart authentication" when user move his mouse over this username.
- We can inspire from Google regarding login screen. I am adding screenshot google-2factor.png for the inspiration. One thing, where we can be better than google could be the "username" link - we can make it more clear that click on it will restart the login.
- We can take a look at Patternfly components and possibly re-use some of them, so we don't need to create our own custom thing

summary: Usability: Improve screen for setup TOTP
description:
The screen for setup TOTP currently looks like this - in the screenshot setup-otp-requiredAction.png . There is the mandatory field for the OTP code and than optional field for the "Device name" where user can specify label of the OTP credential.
Started the thread on keycloak-dev with the topic "Usability: Improve screen for setup TOTP" and so far the conclusions are:
- Keep using "Device name" as the label. Alternatively could be to change to "Phone name", but that would be more work, so sticking to "Device name" could be better
- The "Device name" should be optional in case that user registers first OTP. If he registers second or more OTP, it should be mandatory
- We can display label "One-time code" for the first input field, so both input fields have label. The "One-time code" could be marked with asterisk, so it is clear that it is mandatory. The "Device name" field should be marked with asterisk in case that it is mandatory (which is the case of adding OTP in case that user already has at least one).
- We may add sentence to the point 3 "You can provide a Device Name to help you manage your Authenticator devices." . This sentence is generic enough, so that it can be same sentence displayed in case that Device Name is mandatory or not
- We can add the same sentence above to the tooltip in the old account console in the "Authenticator" tab.

summary: WebAuthn: create authenticator, requiredAction and policy for passwordless
description:
h3. What
Regarding WebAuthn, we need to ensure that user is able to register WebAuthn Security Key as passwordless authenticator (1st factor) or as 2nd factor authenticator. 
In other words, WebAuthn is example of the credential, which is probably useful as both 1st factor or 2nd factor. There may be different requirement for WebAuthn configuration for those 2 cases. For example for passwordless WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "required" in WebAuthn policy and for 2nd factor WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "preferred" .
h3. 
h3. How
Proper solution will be the possibility to create "instances" of credential policy rather than rely on java providers. But until that is done, we will go with a workaround, which may be like this:
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnAuthenticator. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnRegister. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister" . The WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator will be tight to this required action
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnCredentialProvider like "WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider" . It will be used by WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator and WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister.
- Adding another tab in admin console. In addition to the current tab "WebAuthn policy", we will add another tab like "WebAuthn PasswordLess Policy" . The existing tab "WebAuthn Policy" may be renamed to something like "WebAuthn 2nd-factor policy" . The admin will be able to configure different policies for passwordless and different for 2nd factor.
- The previous point means that we may need to add some new set of fields to RealmRepresentation object. All the "webAuthn*" properties may have another counterpart for passwordless. For example "webAuthnPolicyRpEntityName" will have "webAuthnPasswordlessPolicyRpEntityName" .
- The WebAuthnPasswordLessAuthenticator, WebAuthnPasswordLessRegister and WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider will read the configuration from the "passwordless" fields, but otherwise their implementation will be same as for the 2nd factor java classes.
Those points will allow administrator to configure separate policies for 1st-factor and 2nd-factor and add separate authenticators to authentication flow for 1st-factor and 2-nd factor. Also it will allow user to have 2 type of webauthn credentials. Credentials of type "webauthn-passwordless" for 1st factor WebAuthn authentication and "webauthn" for 2nd factor WebAuthn authentication (NOTE: The credential type "webauthn" is already used in latest master, so we will keep it for backwards-compatibility and won't rename it)
This whole thing is a workaround, which will be addressed more properly in the future.

description:
During WebAuthn authentication, we discussed about possible changes like this:
- Don't display the checkboxes of available WebAuthn credentials, which are shown in this slide . Instead of it, automatically try all the WebAuthn credentials of particular user, but just for the particular factor. For example, if WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator is triggered, it will try the WebAuthn passwordless credentials (Credentials of type "webauthn-passwordless"). Otherwise if WebAuthnAuthenticator is triggered, it will try the WebAuthn 2nd factor credentials (Credentials of type "webauthn").
- The attempt to authenticate with WebAuthn (JS call to navigator.credentials.get) will be tried immediately when the page with the WebAuthn authentication is shown. No need for click button "Login" . That's what most other vendors (including Google) do.
- If the attempt of WebAuthn authentication fails, some nice message should be displayed to the user. There will be a possibility to "Try again" and also possibility of "Try another way", but the latter will be displayed just if user has some other alternatives for the 2-factor authentication.
See screenshot google-securityKeyAuthentication.png for an example how Google is displaying the screen for "Try again" or "Try another way"

summary: Refactor login screens to not show many credentials of same type in credential selector
description:
We discussed refactoring of login screens in a way, that credential selector won't show multiple credentials of same type. 
For example assume that user can choose between 3 alternatives when configuring authentication flow: password, OTP and WebAuthn. And assume that particular user john has 1 password, 2 OTP credentials and 2 WebAuthn credentials. Flow is configured as on slide 5 here: . So what will happen is:
- After providing username, user will see the screen with "Password" as that is his preferred credential. No credential selector would be displayed.
- User can click to link "Try another way"
- When he clicks on it, he will be able to choose between "Password", "Authenticator App" (which is OTP) and "Security Key" (which is WebAuthn). The page for OTP will show him available OTP credentials etc.
See slides 4-15 here for more details: .

summary: Allow user to choose from multiple credential types during registration of 2-factor credential during authentication
description:
Let's assume we have authentication flow configured like this:
{code}
Auth type   | Requirement
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cookie   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Kerberos   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
Identity Provider Redirector [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Authenticate with Keycloak [x] Alternative [ ] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - Username Password Form [ ] Alternative [x] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Authenticate with MFA [ ] Alternative [x] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - OTP   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - WebAuthn  [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Hardware Token [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
{code}
Then let's assume that user doesn't yet have any 2-factor credential (OTP or WebAuthn or Hardware Token) configured on his account. So then he should be required to configure either OTP or WebAuthn credential during authentication. In this case, after he finish password authentication, he should be able to choose if he wants to configure OTP or WebAuthn credential and register one of them. He should be able to go back and select different credential (EG. He first clicks on WebAuthn, but then he change his mind because he doesn't have yubikey and his phone doesn't have bluetooth, so he want to go back and register OTP through the Google Authenticator app on his phone)

summary: After password reset, the new password has low priority
description:
Reported by [~tkyjovsk@redhat.com] in KEYCLOAK-11922: after every password update the order of the credential items changes. The newly set password is at the very bottom of the table. Not sure if this is a bug.
Reply by [~mposolda@redhat.com]: yes, the fact that newly updated password is at the very bottom of the table is a bug IMO.
The first credential in the table is "preferred credential" . So for example assume that user has 1 password credential and 1 OTP credential in the table and password is at the top. Then if after updating the password, the password is at the bottom, it means that password is now not preferred credential, but instead the OTP credential is preferred. This could have some side-effects for some authentication flows configurations. The password should ideally remain in same place as it was before.
Will be also good to ensure the same behaviour (password at the same place) is during reset by admin and also when reset by user himself through the account console.

summary: prompt='login' (you are already authenticated)
description:
When using oauth2 to login and prompt='login' is given in the url. Keycloak forces the used to authenticate again. Even if you are already logged in.
So far it works as expected.
But when you change from user A to user B. I get the message:
```
Page has expired
To restart the login process click_here
To continue the login process click_here
```
Then when I click on: `continue the login process` I see this message:
```
You are already authenticated as different user ... in this session. Please log out first
```
I would expect keycloak to handle this gracefully and logout user A when user B authenticates.
If we look at different OAuth2 implementations (github, gitlab, google) they handle this behavior without giving the above error page etc.
To have a smooth user experience I would like keycloak to have the same behavior.

summary: Default Security Headers provider
description:
Keycloak currently has a static list of security headers that are added to HTML responses, but does not have any headers on REST responses. It allows customising the headers directly by setting the header values, which is problematic from the point that headers need to be more dynamic.
We should implement a new default security header provider that follows best practices and allows configuration in terms of high-level configuration options rather than by being able to edit headers directly like the legacy provider does.
One important header that we need to harden is the CSP. We should not allow any inline-scripts or inline-css. For the CSP we most likely need some aspects to be configurable on a per-realm basis.
We also need to consider an option to allow some clients to embed the login form.

summary: [RFE] Authentication -> Flows table: Add the ability to edit flow post adding the flow
description:
Currently it's not possible to edit (sub)flow name / label via the _Actions_ drop-down menu in the _Authentication_ -> _Flows_ table. Once the flow was added to the copy, the only way on how to change the subflow name is to delete it, and add it again with the proper / desired name. Since the subflow definition might contain advanced setup (might contain lot of executions), the need to edit subflow name / label better to reflect actual authentication flow, might be time consuming (the admin needs to delete the original flow, define a new one with desired name, then redefine all of the executions again).
Better approach IMHO would be, if the _Authentication_ -> _Flow_ table would offer _Edit flow_ action within the _Action_ drop-down menu.
*Note:* This RFE is *NOT* about the possibility to rename default flow names. Just about the ability to edit the derived ones, created by the user, from the default ones.

summary: WebAuthn passwordless: use different metadata (label, helpText) than for WebAuthn
description:
h1. What
It will be good if "WebAuthn passwordless" authenticator will use different metadata than "WebAuthn" authenticator for the userDisplayName, userHelpText . Those metadata will be displayed to end-user for example in the select-authenticator screen or in the new account console. It will be good if for WebAuthn passwordless, we display something like "Passwordless Security Key", when for WebAuthn, we display just "Security Key"
h1. How
The PR for KEYCLOAK-12469 adds 3 new metadata methods to the ConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory interface.
The PR for KEYCLOAK-12174 adds new authenticator "WebAuthn Passwordless" .
Some metadata introduced by KEYCLOAK-12469 may need to be different for "WebAuthn Passwordless" than for WebAuthn. For example instead of displayName "Security Key", which is used for the WebAuthn, we may have "Passwordless Security Key" for the WebAuthnPasswordless authenticator.
However none of the PR for KEYCLOAK-12469 and KEYCLOAK-12174 is merged yet. This will need to be postponed until at least one of the PRs is merged (the second then might be updated).
This JIRA is just so that we don't forget to change the metadata.

summary: Support for bulk removal of credentials of particular type
description:
In case that admin decides to not use WebAuthn (or OPT or other credentialType) anymore and he disables WebAuthn authenticators in all authentication flows, it will be ideal if we have some support for bulk removal of all user credentials of particular type.
This may be non-trivial to support. For example we shouldn't automatically clear all OTP credentials just because admin accidentally disabled OTP Authenticator (and enabled it back 1 second after, but credentials are already deleted). So it will be good if some confirmation dialog will be shown to the admin, so it's not that easy to remove all user credentials by accident.

summary: Keycloak Operator: allow creating users without credentials
description:
In Keycloak it is possible to create a user without any credentials (password). This is also what happens when a user logs in via Github: the representation in Keycloak only has a username but no credentials set.
Such users can't currently be created or synced via a KeycloakUser CR, because it doesn't allow to pass empty credentials (and will create random ones if none are provided).

- OOTP is disabled in Reset Credentials flow, so that only password can be changed.

summary: Passwordless WebAuthn Priority
description:
In a Passwordless WebAuthn deployment, it's typically the preferred option, with password + OTP as a fallback in case the user's browser doesn't support it.
However in Keycloak, manual administrator intervention is required to get the WebAuthn prompt to come first. The priority ordering in the Authentication flow configuration is apparently overridden by the user's own credential ordering, and the standard way of enrolling new users (setting a temporary password) always puts Password first.
Suggestions:
* Enable the authentication flow priority to override the user's credential priority.
* Enable the user to configure their own credential priority along with their password, OTP devices, etc.
full_text:
Passwordless WebAuthn Priority

In a Passwordless WebAuthn deployment, it's typically the preferred option, with password + OTP as a fallback in case the user's browser doesn't support it.
However in Keycloak, manual administrator intervention is required to get the WebAuthn prompt to come first. The priority ordering in the Authentication flow configuration is apparently overridden by the user's own credential ordering, and the standard way of enrolling new users (setting a temporary password) always puts Password first.
Suggestions:
* Enable the authentication flow priority to override the user's credential priority.
* Enable the user to configure their own credential priority along with their password, OTP devices, etc.

With current selenium/WebDriver version, which we are using in Keycloak master (Selenium 3.14.0) , it is not much possible to test WebAuthn. The only option is Chrome browser and Chrome testing API, which is currently used in some existing WebAuthn tests (EG. WebAuthnRegisterAndLoginTest ). Some more advanced WebAuthn features are not possible to test at all with Chrome Testing API (Resident keys, User verification with value REQUIRED, etc)
With the newest Selenium/WebDriver, there should be better support for WebAuthn testing. It will hopefully allow to simulate various WebAuthn "authenticators" with various setups and allow to test advanced WebAuthn features, error scenarios (See KEYCLOAK-12859 for some example error scenarios) etc.
h2. How
This JIRA is to:
- Prototype the WebAuthn testing with latest Selenium and verify what capabilities it provides.
- Based on that, we may try to update the Keycloak testsuite to latest Selenium. This may involve some more dependency updates (Arquillian, Drone etc).

Use newest WebDriver/Selenium for the WebAuthn testing

summary: Ability to order credentials in the new account console
description:
- In the new account console, user should be able to select preferred "Default" authenticator for two-factor authentication.
- User should be also able to select preferred option for the 1st factor authentication. For example if we prefer to authenticate with the "Password" or with "WebAuthn passwordless".
Ordering of credentials is already possible at the model level and is doable in the admin console (User -> Credentials tab). In the new account console, it may need to be done differently due the fact that there are "categories" as well in the UI.

description:
This epic is switch WebAuthn feature from "preview" to supported. There are few more pre-requisities to allow WebAuthn as being supported. This includes some work related to other epics:
1) KEYCLOAK-13131 - Improve on WebAuthn automated testing
2) KEYCLOAK-13139 - Support for more advanced scenarios like attestation statement verification or retrieve of WebAuthn metadata
3) KEYCLOAK-13136 - More flexibility around configuration of required actions and authenticators for WebAuthn. PAsswordless WebAuthn etc
4) New Account console and Account REST API should be supported as WebAuthn management by end users is available in new account console only (not in the old legacy account console)
5) Wait for more feedback from customers and eventually do some more bugfixing
This epic will contain tasks, which are not related to any of the epics mentioned in first 3 points and some general improvements required to have WebAuthn supported.

summary: [SPIKE] Plan for third-party cookie blocking
description:
Safari has already started blocking third-party cookies [1], and other browser will follow suite in the future [2]. 
Third-party cookies are leveraged within keycloak.js especially for session logout notification, as well as often used in SPA type applications for silent refresh. We have for a long type provided support for refresh tokens in keycloak.js, which reduces the implication of this, but we do need to deprecate/remove features that require third-party cookies.
We should also start considering how we can recommend SPA type applications with a backend service that handles the flows, which is slightly more secure as refresh tokens are not exposed to the browser.
[1] 
[2]

summary: Multiple errors: readiness and shutdown checks
description:
The existing readiness check ({{org.keycloak.testsuite.arquillian.containers.KeycloakQuarkusServerDeployableContainer#waitForReadiness}}) has proven to be unreliable on Quarkus, in part because REST endpoints are brought up before the actual startup has completed. This leads to multiple test errors.
A prototype based on MicroProfile Health has shown much better results. As soon as MP Health support lands in Keycloak, the testsuite should be ported to MP Health too. Additionally, {{container.waitFor()}} should be added to the {{stop()}} method to avoid false positives in {{waitForReadiness()}}.

summary: Test error: org.keycloak.testsuite.admin.ServerInfoTest#testServerInfo
Specify Signature Algorithm in Signed JWT Client Authentication
description:
The current keycloak verifies the signed JWT by using the signature algorithm that this signed JWT's JOSE header's "alg" field tells.
This seems to be not secure because the client can use the algorithm that is considered to be not secure(e.g. RS256) and the keycloak accepts it.
Therefore, the allowed signature algorithm for Signed JWT client authentication can be set in advance expilcitly according to the client metadata "token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg" defined by OIDC Client Dynamic Registration (
Keycloak refuses the signed JWT that is signed by using the signature algorithm other than this registered signature algorithm.
For backward compatibility, if this allowed signature algorithm is not set, keycloak works as it is.

description:
To make it easy to secure client applications, it is beneficial to realize the following three points in a unified way.
1. Setting policies on what configuration a client can have
2. Validation of client configurations
3. Conformance to a profile such as FAPI
1 and 2 have been realized by the current keycloak, but not flexible and comprehensive.
To realize these three points in a unified way, here "Client Policies" concept is introduced.
3 will be realized by [Client Conformance Profiles| based on this "Client Policies". It discusses which kind of security profiles like FAPI are supported and how to implement them.

summary: Valid Redirect URI for review apps (wildcard in hostname?)
description:
I'm using gitlab to handle code and it has this great feature called "review apps". This feature makes every feature branch deployed to a site so interested parties can review it before it is merged. So if you create a new branch called "my-cool-feature" it will automatically deploy to a site called "my-cool-feature.myapp.mycompany.com".
Now I wanted to use review apps with an application that is protected by keycloak. Everything worked great until I got to the Valid Redirect URI part. I previously did not understand that it only accepted a wildcard at the end. The origin URI accepts wildcards in the hostname so I found it natural that redirect uri would too. However after reading the documentation I found this section:
> Wildcards ( * ) are only allowed at the end of a URI, i.e. 
So my question is if there is any possibility to add a feature that allows for use with this kind of dynamic sites. I cannot really predict all the feature branch names that developers will create so they cannot really be pre-registered. If valid redirect URI would allow for something like that would solve it directly. I found some previous discussions about having a wildcard in the host part:
Of course there are the usual security concerns etc. I think having a wildcard in the host of valid redirect uri would be really useful for some development scenarios but should probably not be used in production. It would be nice if I as a server admin could make that decision though, instead of not having the option at all. Also I think with the cloud, container, and k8s environments we have today everything is more dynamic, sites are created and deleted on a daily basis with potentially dynamic hostnames. So having this function today is probably more motivated than back in 2016.
However, my scenario is just using keycloak to secure these review apps that appear on dynamic sites. If there is a different way to achieve it other than allowing wildcards in the hostname I could use that instead :-).

Prepare Keycloak and adapters for those changes and document the features that are affected by it and can't be fixed.

summary: Test for database compatibility
description:
Similarly to KEYCLOAK-14141, a test for Liquibase compatibility will be developed to test database compatibility. The test should do something along these lines:
# Run old version on a database
# Shutdown old version
# Inspect DATABASECHANGELOG table
# Run new version on the same database
# Shutdown new version
# Inspect new items in DATABASECHANGELOG table
If the last step reveals new items, database compatibility is at risk. There could be some permitted actions though (e.g. {{createIndex}}) that would not signal database incompatibility.

summary: Unable to add more than 6 acceptable AAGUIDs for WebAuthn
description:
h2. Summary
Only 6 AAGUIDs can be added to the Acceptable AAGUID field under WebAuthn Policy of the Keycloak Admin Console because the underlying database column only allows 255 characters. We should be able to whitelist more than 6 AAGUIDs. 
h2. Details
An authenticator device used by WebAuthn contains an AAUID that can be used to identify the type of the authenticator. Each AAGUID is 36 characters long including hyphens (ex. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). 
These AAGUID can be whitelisted in Keycloak Admin Console via Authentication -> WebAuthn Policy -> Acceptable AAGUIDs. This list of AAGUIDs is then converted into one comma separated string by org.keycloak.models.jpa.RealmAdapter.setWebAuthnPolicy() then inserted into the "value" column of "realm_attribute" table in Keycloak's database. 
However, because this column is only 255 characters long, only six AAGUID can be added (6 x 36 AAGUID characters + 5 commas = 221 total characters). Adding more than 6 will fail with an error message. 
There should be support for whitelisting more than 6 AAGUIDs.

summary: Support for generating SSL keystore before running testsuite
description:
h2. Why
In order to properly test cookies Keycloak needs to be bound to a different hostname than localhost because localhost is taken as an exception by many browsers and therefore has less strict rules for cookies.
We'll use services like nip.io as the most straightforward solution that doesn't require any environment modifications (like {{/etc/hosts}} or DNS). However, in order not to be dependent on a single externally hosted service that would be hardcoded in the tests, it will be possible to set the hostname prior to running test using a CLI argument.
h2. What
Add support for updating (or generating a new) SSL keystore and truststore in testsuite before running tests. Use {{auth.server.host}} (and probably {{app.server.host}} as well) properties add them trusted hostnames.
h2. How
Use either a [Maven plugin| or do this directly in some abstract test class.

summary: Avoid creating default keys during startup
description:
We changed the startup to avoid creating default keys during startup. See 
However, for Quarkus, this is not working properly when starting the server for the very first time and authenticating for the first time after creating the admin user.
After that, the server behaves normally and no more errors are shown in logs.
The error that occurs is a {{ClassCastException}} from Hibernate saying that the {{ClientEntity}} can not be cast to {{Serializable}}. And changing {{ClientEntity}} to implement {{Serializable}} gives another exception saying that the "id types mismatch, expected String but got ClientEntity".
In order to reduce startup time, we should fix this error and remove the code to generate default keys just like in the main distribution (KEYCLOAK-14299)

summary: Remove bi-directional associations and eager initialization of entity properties
description:
We don't need to eagerly initialize entity properties when they are collections. That should be done by Hibernate and we don't want to create unnecessary instances when Hibernate is creating instances of our entities.
We also should avoid having bi-directional associations so that we can leverage some enhancements that Hibernate does in the latest versions in regards to lazy loading associations.
In regards to entity enhancements, Hibernate (and mainly in Quarkus) does not seem to work well with bi-directional associations. In addition to that, in most cases we don't even need this type of association but just the key used for the association.
full_text:
Remove bi-directional associations and eager initialization of entity properties

We also should avoid having bi-directional associations so that we can leverage some enhancements that Hibernate does in the latest versions in regards to lazy loading associations.
In regards to entity enhancements, Hibernate (and mainly in Quarkus) does not seem to work well with bi-directional associations. In addition to that, in most cases we don't even need this type of association but just the key used for the association.

summary: [Admin console] Improve the save strategy around the console
description:
When users finish creating an IdP, this provider will be published to the log in screens at once. But the configuration is not completed in fact. There are still some settings that need to be made, e.g. advanced settings, mappers, etc. If there are some users log in through the provider now, they will meet errors. 
We need to improve the save strategy to make this flow more reasonable.

summary: Polish My Resource Page (some more)
description:
From review of 
I've, however, found a few bugs.
When you unshare a resource, the change doesn't take effect in the UI imediately. It still says that "Resource is share with ...".
It's not possible to unshare a resource for a selected user (well, technically it is, but you need to remove all scopes from given user which is not very intuitive). When you unshare, it's unshared for all users. If the button is really supposed to unshare all, it should explicitly say so and there should be a warning modal dialog.
When a user is not found, a generic "Not Found" alert is displayed after the Share dialog is closed. There are two problems with that. 1) "Not Found" is not explanatory enough (should be perhaps "User XY was not found". 2) When you share a resource with multiple users at once, only a success alert is displayed. User is not informed at all that some other user was not found and resource is not shared. We probably check for user existence when adding them using the "Add" button in the dialog.
The Permission requests dialog doesn't seem to work at all! Accept/Deny doesn't do anything.
Also, there are still some valid issues stated in the original JIRA.
There are still some missing capitals. "C" in "close" in permissions request dialog. "P" in "permissions requested" in the same dialog. "P" in "permissions" in Shared with me table.
Permission request dialog doesn't show Requestor.

summary: Welcome cards should be driven by content.js
description:
The cards on the Welcome Page should be driven by the data in That way, you don't have to manually repeat the same data in index.ftl and the Welcome Page will be automatically updated whenever someone adds a page to the application.

 * icon name
 * image url (not sure if this is a good idea but it would be nice if you could use an image instead of an icon)

summary: Make ClientProvider independent of RealmProvider
description:
h2. What
Currently the {{ClientProvider}} interface. Make the two independent of each other, i.e. extract client provider from the realm store and ensure there are no foreign keys in the database to clients.
h2. Why
Store.x assumes that there will be loose coupling between the different stores. The current database model of the client store is tightly coupled with that of the realm, and thus the code often references realm provider where a client provider should have been used.

summary: Reset Credentials Flow does not delete existing OTP
description:
With a default installation of the latest keycloak version also any previous version with flow contains a conditional action to when the user has 2FA enabled.
That means when the user chooses he will first need to reconfigure the OTP and after that choose a new password.
During the action, the existing authenticator should be deleted. This is not what is happening currently. Instead the existing authenticator is kept and an additional authenticator is created.
The user is not aware of this and will generally choose the same name for the authenticator as he used before. Thus he will be unable to differentiate between the old and new authenticators. I.e. after resetting his password the user will have a hard time logging in.
Even if the user was so lucky as to use a new name for the authenticator, he will be confused by having to select which authenticator to use, when one is obsolete.
This issue is somewhat related to KEYCLOAK-13134.
full_text:
Reset Credentials Flow does not delete existing OTP

With a default installation of the latest keycloak version also any previous version with flow contains a conditional action to when the user has 2FA enabled.
That means when the user chooses he will first need to reconfigure the OTP and after that choose a new password.
During the action, the existing authenticator should be deleted. This is not what is happening currently. Instead the existing authenticator is kept and an additional authenticator is created.
The user is not aware of this and will generally choose the same name for the authenticator as he used before. Thus he will be unable to differentiate between the old and new authenticators. I.e. after resetting his password the user will have a hard time logging in.
Even if the user was so lucky as to use a new name for the authenticator, he will be confused by having to select which authenticator to use, when one is obsolete.
This issue is somewhat related to KEYCLOAK-13134.

summary: Improvements to re-authentication flows
description:
In cases where the user is requested to re-authenticate the username is shown as an input field (some times empty I think). If the user enters a different username than the currently authenticated user an error message is displayed: "You are already authenticated as different user". This is not very good usability.
Examples of cases when a user can be requested to re-authenticate includes:
* login=prompt in an OIDC flow
* max_age in an OIDC flow
* An AIA is triggered, which requires re-auth
The proposed solution here is to display the details of the logged-in user with an option to restart the authentication process, similar to what we do on the OTP screen already:
 !screenshot-1.png|thumbnail! 
If a AIA is being triggered, the AIA should be cancelled (including kc_action_status=cancelled in the response to the app).
We also need to consider cases where password is not the first step that is presented to the user. Example of these include webauthn passwordless, identity broker, etc.. These should also have the "Not you" option, or in cases like the identity brokering most likely the correct solution is to simply destroy the session and create a new session if the user is changed.
full_text:

Examples of cases when a user can be requested to re-authenticate includes:

* max_age in an OIDC flow

The proposed solution here is to display the details of the logged-in user with an option to restart the authentication process, similar to what we do on the OTP screen already:

If a AIA is being triggered, the AIA should be cancelled (including kc_action_status=cancelled in the response to the app).
We also need to consider cases where password is not the first step that is presented to the user. Example of these include webauthn passwordless, identity broker, etc.. These should also have the "Not you" option, or in cases like the identity brokering most likely the correct solution is to simply destroy the session and create a new session if the user is changed.

summary: Add --verbose and --force options to the Wildfly upgrade automated script
description:
* By default, the Wildfly upgrade automated script upgrades version of the particular Keycloak artifact (POM property, adapter dependency, or some other common XML element, shared with Wildfly application server) _*ONLY*_ if the new version of the element is _*HIGHER*_ than the current of the corresponding element found in the local copy of the Keycloak repository. But also in this case the script prints out (in a loglevel of _*DEBUG*_) the reason, why the element in question wasn't updated. Currently, there doesn't exist and easy option for the user to change the log level from _*INFO*_ (default one) to _*DEBUG*_ one, to see this kind of message. *Therefore add _-v_ / _--verbose_ new CLI option to the script, so it's possible to inspect these messages,
* Moreover, add a _-f_ / _--force_ combination of options to the script to instruct the script to allow to replace newer version of a particular Keycloak characteristic (POM property, adapter dependency etc.) with an older version. In other words perform, actually perform a Keycloak downgrade to (some of) previous Wildfly versions. This is necessary to be able to add tests for the script (the test to check e.g. if _git diff_ produced for upgrade to Wildfly e.g. 16 matches the manually created diff / code change, that already exists in the Keycloak repository).

But also in this case the script prints out (in a loglevel of _*DEBUG*_) the reason, why the element in question wasn't updated. Currently, there doesn't exist and easy option for the user to change the log level from _*INFO*_ (default one) to _*DEBUG*_ one, to see this kind of message. *Therefore add _-v_ / _--verbose_ new CLI option to the script, so it's possible to inspect these messages,
* Moreover, add a _-f_ / _--force_ combination of options to the script to instruct the script to allow to replace newer version of a particular Keycloak characteristic (POM property, adapter dependency etc.) with an older version. In other words perform, actually perform a Keycloak downgrade to (some of) previous Wildfly versions. This is necessary to be able to add tests for the script (the test to check e.g. if _git diff_ produced for upgrade to Wildfly e.g. 16 matches the manually created diff / code change, that already exists in the Keycloak repository).

summary: Use third party Postgresql Operator by default
description:
h2. Motivation
Keycloak Operator uses embedded Postgresql database by default. This approach is not maintainable for the future as our team doesn't have enough expertise to run Postgresql in production. In order to solve this, we need to migrate to an external database by default.
h2. Design
The implementation will be divided into a few stages:
* Adding additional fields to the Keycloak CR that makes the user experience better.
* Flipping the switch to support the external database by default
* Dropping database backup functionality altogether
* Updating the CSVs in Operatorhub
Depending on the timing, all this may happen in Keycloak 13.0.0.
The summary of the proposed changes might be found here: 
The main mechanism behind this feature will remain the same. The Operator will sync the database address and credentials with leveraging the current implementation of the external database connection.
h2. Risks
This also needs to be discussed with Operator SDK Team. As far as I know, we will be one of the first Operators planning this move.
h2. Open questions
None.

summary: Enhance type checking within AbstractStorageManager
description:
Currently, it is possible to obtain a storage provider that implements some interface. However, we should have some enhanced type checking which would check, at compile-time, for example, that the required interface is a supertype of GroupStorageProvider/UserStorageProvider, etc. This is related to too general definition of [ComponentFactory interface| which could be also adjusted with some limitation to _CreateType_ (Some relation with _ProviderType_).
There is an example of [how it could look like| in the future. However, this work is currently blocked by KEYCLOAK-14750.

summary: Create clients in Keycloak for each OAuthClient resource
description:
h2. Motivation
OpenShift uses 2 mechanisms for managing oAuth Clients:
- Service Accounts (see [the documentation|
- OAuthClient resources (see [the REST API|
The goal of this ticket is to create Keycloak Clients based on new OAuthClient showing up.
h2. Design
To be discussed. However, there are two ways of doing that:
- Observe OAuthClients from an Operator and create KeycloakClient CRs on the fly
- Enhance {{OpenshiftClientStorageProvider}} to support this use case as well.
The latter approach has one downside though. It requires the Keycloak instance to reside in the OpenShift cluster to obtain both {{ca.crt}} and an {{access token}} for Kube API. The Operator seems like a bit more flexible approach.
h3. Rough estimate
1-2 weeks for 1 person.
h3. Open questions
The most important question is what kind of architecture fits here. Can we assume that Keycloak will always be deployed in OpenShift? If not than using an Operator supporting external Keycloak would be a way to go.

summary: Add tests for the Wildfly upgrade automated script
description:
Automated script is used to produce necessary Keycloak repository changes, when upgrading Keycloak to a next version of Wildfly.
While the changes are reviewed prior submitting a final PR, we need tests for the automated script (have some way to rely the repository changes produced by the script match earlier changes, done for upgrading Keycloak to previous versions of Wildfly, e.g. Wildfly 16 etc.)
The expectation (expected output) is the Keycloak repository changes produced by the script corresponding changes of all necessary files, that were previously done when performing a manual update. The output can actually contain more changes (if some specific area of Keycloak repository wasn't updated as part of that upgrade to Wildfly -- some changes got forgotten etc.).
But script output shouldn't contain less changes than were done by manual upgrade.

Add tests for the Wildfly upgrade automated script

Automated script is used to produce necessary Keycloak repository changes, when upgrading Keycloak to a next version of Wildfly.
