summary: Wildfly upgrade automated script - Align Python artifact version comparsion algorithm with the Maven / Java one
description:
Currently, the automated script to upgrade Keycloak to next Wildfly version uses Python's [_packaging.version.parse_| method to compare artifact versions (decide if version of specific artifact needs to be updated or not).
But in some cases [*], the version comparison result produced by Python differs from the result produced by the Maven's / Java's [_ComparableVersion_ implementation| of the version comparison algorithm.
[*] One specific example of different / differing output is when comparing artifact of the same version, but the second one suffixed with some _redhat-*_ suffix (in this case Python considers the version without the suffix as the higher one, while Maven / Java considers as the higher one the suffixed one). But there might be more cases, when the comparison result differs.
Therefore, update the automated script to use Python's implementation of the aforementioned Maven _ComparableVersion_ algorithm.
full_text:
Wildfly upgrade automated script - Align Python artifact version comparsion algorithm with the Maven / Java one

Currently, the automated script to upgrade Keycloak to next Wildfly version uses Python's [_packaging.version.parse_| method to compare artifact versions (decide if version of specific artifact needs to be updated or not).
But in some cases [*], the version comparison result produced by Python differs from the result produced by the Maven's / Java's [_ComparableVersion_ implementation| of the version comparison algorithm.
[*] One specific example of different / differing output is when comparing artifact of the same version, but the second one suffixed with some _redhat-*_ suffix (in this case Python considers the version without the suffix as the higher one, while Maven / Java considers as the higher one the suffixed one). But there might be more cases, when the comparison result differs.
Therefore, update the automated script to use Python's implementation of the aforementioned Maven _ComparableVersion_ algorithm.

summary: Mount custom resources and configuration with Keycloak Operator
description:
h2. Motivation
One of the main goals of the Operator is to provide an opinionated way of setting a Keycloak cluster up. This effectively means that an optimized configuration for a given use case should be provided out of the box. Nevertheless, recent RHMI production failure along with multiple feature requests from Keycloak Community showed many production hotfixes (and workarounds) require supplying:
- Custom container Args (that translate into Java System Properties)
- Custom environment variables
- Custom modifications to standalone[-ha].xml (that translates into autorun scripts in our Container).
The design need to add all of the above pain points and the following use cases:
- Mounting additional CAs
- Mounting Keytabs (requires additional work, see KEYCLOAK-15558 and KEYCLOAK-15784)
- Feature toggles
- Configuring proxy settings
- Configuring custom providers (the ones that user deploy).

summary: Option "version" of the "kc.sh config" command
description:
Environment: Keycloak 12-SNAPSHOT with quarkus 1.9.0.CR1
It seems "--version" should not be displayed in the help to "config" command?
{code}
$ ./kc.sh config --help
 ... BIG OUTPUT WITH LOTS OF COMMANDS AND CONFIG OPTIONS ...
--proxy=<value> 	The proxy mode if the server is behind a reverse proxy. Possible values are: none, edge, reencrypt, and passthrough.
-V, --version 	Print version information and exit.
--verbose  Print out more details when running this command.
{code}
This implies to me that "--version" is one of the arguments, which I can pass to the "config" command. Hence trying it:
{code}
$ ./kc.sh config --version
{code}
And there is no output at all, which is confusing behaviour.

description:
We will need PR sent to keycloak/keycloak-documentation. This will require:
- Update of some versions for Wildfly and various other components. See this PR for the inspiration, which was used for Wildfly 16 upgrade: 
- Update in the migration guide with the stuff specific for the current Wildfly version. See this PR for the inspiration: 
- Possibly some other documentation parts, which require updates, based on the things specific to particular Wildfly version update, which needed to be changed in the codebase. For Wildfly 20, there will be a need to update cross-dc documentation as there will be some changes needed. The infinispan-server version used for cross-dc integration is 9.4.18.Final (different than the infinispan version used by the Keycloak server itself, which is infinispan 10.1.8.Final ). Due to this, there will be a need to set "protocolVersion" as 2.9 in the remote-store elements used in the documentation.

summary: Upstream Bundle Format - Convert old versions in operator-framework/community-operators
description:
Generally, bundle format is a slightly different way of storing our operator's installation metadata, and providing it to OpenShift. "appregistry" was the previous format, and many of its same YAMLs continue to be used, with some extra files added. For more context, see all JIRAs entitled "Upstream Bundle Format - *", see also [this documentation|
Specifically for this JIRA, we need to implement the changes specified by [this issue| in the shared upstream Github repo [operator-framework/community-operators|
# Use the tool [opm| to convert our 7 old keycloak operator versions in 
[community-operators/upstream-community-operators/keycloak-operator/|
# Remove package.yaml, to signal that the bundle conversion has been performed to the operator-framework team's automation.

summary: Remote Infinispan connection
description:
h2. Motivation
In order to support Cross Site Replication (and Keycloak.x in general) Keycloak needs to be able to connect to a remote Infinispan/RHDG Cluster managed by the Infinispan/RHDG Operator.
h2. Design
Designing interaction between the Infinispan and Keycloak Operators require separating concerns:
* An administrator or a third party user is responsible for spinning Infinispan cluster up by using Infinispan Operator and [Infinispan CR| The configuration includes Cross Site Replication settings.
* An administrator or a third party user is responsible for spinning Keycloak cluster up by using Keycloak Operator and [Keycloak CR| The CR will be altered to contain a pointer to the Infinispan CR and other necessary settings.
Keycloak cluster will connect to the Infinispan cluster using a Kubernetes Service. This means the Infinispan Operator will be able to perform reconfiguration or upgrade procedure transparently to Keycloak instances. 
In order to avoid the circular dependency problem between Keycloak and Infinispan Operators, the initial prototype will not use Remote Store authentication nor encryption.
In order to support the functionality, the Keycloak CR will require the following modifications:
{code}
apiVersion: keycloak.org/v1alpha1
kind: Keycloak
metadata:
 name: example-keycloak
 labels:
 app: sso
spec:
 externalInfinispan:
 # A label selector similar to the one from Realm, Client and User CR
 instanceSelector:
 matchLabels:
 app: infinispan
{code}
Once external Infinispan is detected, the Keycloak Operator will create Infinispan [Cache CRs| for all required caches. The Cache CRs will not be reconciled (just in case some manual changes will be needed) - they will use a {{CreateAction}} only.
Things to be done (bottom up):
- Modify the Keycloak Container to support external Infinispan cluster. The implementation should be done as CLI scripts activated on certain environmental variables.
- Implement similar functionality for RHSSO.
- Implement CRD changes in the Operator.
- Create Cache CRs by the Operator when an external Infinispan is detected.
- Leverage the newly created options (for external Infinispan) in Keycloak and RHSSO images
h2. Open questions
* What will happen when Infinispan is down?
* Should we take Infinispan health probes into consideration when checking Keyclaok readiness probes?

summary: Get rid of manual calling of commit method
description:
This happens in several places, for example, here:

summary: Implement remote Infinispan support in Keycloak container
description:
The motivation and overall design for this ticket has been provided in KEYCLOAK-16168
The aim of this task is to enable Keycloak to connect to a Remote Infinispan cluster, which is activated on {{REMOTE_INFINISPAN_ADDRESS}} property. Once the property is provided, the scripts should reconfigure all caches (along with [the documentation| The implementation should also support setting authentication settings as well as pointing a truststore for encryption. Here's an example of such configuration:
{code}
<system-properties>
 <property name="hotrod.auth_username" value="${env.REMOTE_INFINISPAN_USERNAME}"/>
 <property name="hotrod.auth_password" value="${env.REMOTE_INFINISPAN_PASSWORD}"/>
 <property name="hotrod.auth_realm" value="REMOTE_INFINISPAN_AUTH_REALM" />
 <property name="hotrod.auth_server_name" value="REMOTE_INFINISPAN_AUTH_SERVER_NAME"/>
 <property name="hotrod.sasl_mechanism" value="DIGEST-MD5"/>
 <property name="hotrod.trust_store_path" value="/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/service-ca.crt" />
 <property name="jboss.site.name" value="REMOTE_INFINISPAN_SITE_NAME"/>
</system-properties>
....
<distributed-cache name="clientSessions" owners="1">
 <remote-store cache="client-sessions" remote-servers="remote-cache" passivation="false" fetch-state="false" purge="false" preload="false" shared="true">
 <property name="rawValues">true</property>
 <property name="marshaller">org.keycloak.cluster.infinispan.KeycloakHotRodMarshallerFactory</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.auth_username">${hotrod.auth_username}</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.auth_password">${hotrod.auth_password}</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.auth_realm">${hotrod.auth_realm}</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.auth_server_name">${hotrod.auth_server_name}</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.sasl_mechanism">${hotrod.sasl_mechanism}</property>
 <property name="infinispan.client.hotrod.trust_store_path">${hotrod.trust_store_path}</property>
 </remote-store>
</distributed-cache>
{code}

summary: Many realms: Background tasks try to cache all realms
description:
h2. What
When testing with 500-1000 realms, I can see the stacktrace like below (section "Stacktrace") from time to time. The reason is that background tasks (ClearExpiredEvents, ClearExpiredUserSessions) iterate over all realms and try to cache them. The attempt to cache each realm causes lots of SQL calls to the DB as the realm are cached "eagerly" (all the entities are loaded from DB to be allow to fully cache realm). More details in the CachedRealm constructor.
I've tested with Keycloak 9 (RHSSO 7.4). The latest Keycloak master has some changes related to model, however I suppose this issue exists in the master as well (Not 100% sure).
This can maybe affect performance tests triggered for server HTTP requests, which can be slower due the lots of DB calls needed to cache all the realms. But not 100% sure
h2. Workaround
Make sure that standalone.xml is re-configured for example like this:
{code}
<scheduled-task-interval>9000</scheduled-task-interval>
{code}
But this can have other side-effects (lots of dead sessions etc)
h2. Possible solution
Probably short-term (Long term might be new store improvements):
- Background tasks don't try to "cache the world", but just do their jobs
- Caching of the realm itself is improved like:
-- Not cache whole realm in single step. For example re-use DefaultLazyLoader , which is already used for users?
-- Not so much "boilerplate" entities needed for each realm (EG. 5 authentication flows and much more authentication executions even if authentication flows are unchanged)

summary: Check if ClearExpiredUserSessions can be optimized or removed
description:
The ClearExpiredUserSessions is background task periodically triggered. When it is in progress, it does lots of possible uneffective operations and unecessary network calls. This can have the impact on performance.
The issues are:
- It iterates over all userSessions and then remove them one-by-one. Same for remoteCache (in case that cross-dc integration is enabled). The ideal is, that the method UserSessionProvider.removeExpired is removed entirely. Which means that when we add/update userSession and clientSession entities, we may need to use the "cache.put" or "cache.replace" operations with the expiration/maxIdle parameters. This would mean that infinispan (JDG for the remoteCache) will take care of removing expired entities. This probably applies to offline sessions and loginFailure entities as well.
- Same can be done for authenticationSessions (That is not so urgent as it is not applicable for JDG and hopefully authenticationSessions will be local, but still will be good to do)
- UserSessionPersister.removeExpired needs to be fixed as well to avoid iterating over all realms. Can be done as part of KEYCLOAK-16802
- All the issues above are especially bad in case there is big number of realms as periodic tasks iterate over all realms. When this JIRA and KEYCLOAK-16802 is fixed, iterating over all realms can be avoided.

The infinispan-server version used for cross-dc integration is 9.4.18.Final (different than the infinispan version used by the Keycloak server itself, which is infinispan 10.1.8.Final ). Due to this, there will be a need to set "protocolVersion" as 2.9 in the remote-store elements used in the documentation.

summary: Improve performance of ClearExpiredEvents background task
description:
ClearExpiredEvents background task currently does two things, which are bad for performance.
- Iterates over all realms and adds all realms to the cache if they are not yet there. 
- It clear events in the separate SQL query for each realm. So with 5000 realms, which have events persistence enabled, task triggers 5000 SQL calls to delete expired events
full_text:
Improve performance of ClearExpiredEvents background task

ClearExpiredEvents background task currently does two things, which are bad for performance.
- Iterates over all realms and adds all realms to the cache if they are not yet there. 
- It clear events in the separate SQL query for each realm. So with 5000 realms, which have events persistence enabled, task triggers 5000 SQL calls to delete expired events

summary: Improve performance of JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired
description:
The JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired is currently called from ClearExpiredUserSessions. It is called separately for each realm and it calls 2 SQL to delete expired entities. Hence for deployment with 5K realms, there are 10K SQL commands called to delete expired sessions.
Moreover ClearExpiredUserSessions needs to iterate over all realms, which is bad performance - will be fixed together with KEYCLOAK-16755
full_text:
Improve performance of JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired

The JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired is currently called from ClearExpiredUserSessions. It is called separately for each realm and it calls 2 SQL to delete expired entities. Hence for deployment with 5K realms, there are 10K SQL commands called to delete expired sessions.
Moreover ClearExpiredUserSessions needs to iterate over all realms, which is bad performance - will be fixed together with KEYCLOAK-16755

summary: Summarization of 7.5 release elements
full_text: Summarization of 7.5 release elements

description:
Tree store is an abstraction layer on various storage implementations that provides a unified view on the underlying storages that provide persistence or caching. The aim is to hide details of caching / federation / persistence setup from the code reading and writing objects like users, groups etc.
It has to be able to form a tree from given an implementations of a and provide wiring to allow for caching, invalidation, reads and writes.
In the following example, the caching layer is realized via infinispan, storage is joining LDAP and REST interface to SCIM, with additional attributes stored in JPA store. Each of the Infinispan, LDAP, SCIM and JPA federation would have separate implementation 
!Map storage - stacking.png!
In essence, this task is about creating boilerplate code that allows wiring various storages to form a storage capable of leveraging various storage technologies (database, LDAP, Infinispan, ...) for storage and caching objects. This task is not about implementing the storages themselves.

summary: Support for amphibian (both component and standalone) provider
description:
Currently a only act as a standalone provider, or a [component provider factory| This is inconvenient since the configuration of the factory is done via two different mechanisms (once via method {{init}}, once via parameter passed to {{create}} method).
This task is to add support for _amphibian provider factories_ that would be able to act both as component and standalone provider factory. In either case, new {{Provider}} would be obtained by call to {{create(KeycloakSession)}} method, removing the need for distinguishing the two cases.

Support for amphibian (both component and standalone) provider

Currently a only act as a standalone provider, or a [component provider factory| This is inconvenient since the configuration of the factory is done via two different mechanisms (once via method {{init}}, once via parameter passed to {{create}} method).

summary: Username or email field is cleared in registration form when it is duplicate
description:
There is an UX problem in Registration form. When username or email is duplicate then registration form is reshown with relevant error message, which is OK. But username or email field is blank in this case, so user can't patch value easily but have to retype it Common practice in forms with good UX is reshowning values so user can patch them (except password fields naturally).
 is in {{validate()}} method of the {{org.keycloak.authentication.forms.RegistrationUserCreation}} and {{org.keycloak.authentication.forms.RegistrationProfile}} where these fields are explicitly cleared on error

summary: Apply workaround for WFCORE-5335
description:
The [fix| for [WFCORE-5241| is [known not to work properly| on Linux systems derived from Debian distribution, where [_/bin/sh_ is configured to point to _dash_ (the Debian Almquist Shell)| (thus the case of e.g. _Ubuntu 20.04_ release or the Ubuntu based images, utilized by [Keycloak's GitHub actions|
The [original Wildfly Core patch got already reverted| in Wildfly Core upstream. But we need to apply a workaround till the reverted patch propagates from Wildfly Core's _master_ branch to next major release / tag.

{noformat}
$ mvn clean install -nsu -B -e -DskipTests -Pquarkus,distribution
{noformat}

$ mvn clean install -nsu -B -e -f testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server -Pauth-server-quarkus

{noformat}

summary: Refactor KeycloakSessionFactory
description:
Currently there are {{ProviderFactory}} and {{ComponentFactory}} that basically do the same thing, and {{AmphibianProviderFactory}} introduced in KEYCLOAK-17409 glues the two together to allow for survival of {{ComponentFactory}} instances across request and consistent creation of the {{Provider}} s regardless of whether the originating factory is {{ComponentFactory}} or {{ProviderFactory}}.
This is however a temporary solution that should eventually be replaced by a refactored {{KeycloakSessionFactory}} that potentially renames components and removes the need for distinct {{ComponentFactory}} and {{ProviderFactory}}, thus removing the need for {{AmphibianProviderFactory}}.

summary: Replace EQ operator with HAS_VALUE operator
description:
The {{EQ}} operator as we have it now often doesn't reflect the real meaning behind to constraint we are trying to achieve. This happens in case we are trying to filter entities based on some list attribute, for example, we want to filter users that have a role with id 1 assigned. 
In this case the resulting ModelCriteriaBuilder constraint looks as follows: {{mcb.compare(ASSIGNED_ROLE_ID, EQ, 1)}}, which doesn't correspond with verbal constraint: {{I want all users that have role with id 1 assigned}}. This may be causing confusion for any newcomers to Keycloak codebase.
Therefore, we propose changing {{EQ}} operator to {{HAS_VALUE}} that can be verbally mapped to both is equal to a value and list has item.

summary: Improve auth_time handling throughout Keycloak
description:
h2. Why
Currently, the auth_time in Keycloak is handled incorrectly. Auth_time should be taken as the time the user entered the credentials, in other words when they actively participated in the authentication process. The current status is that Keycloak sets auth_time to current time in every auth flow except when the user is authenticated using SSO cookie.
*NOTE:* auth_time in this context is the [internal Keycloak variable| not necessarily the OIDC claim even though it's closely related.
h2. What
Reconsider how the auth_time is handled for all protocols and authenticators. Keycloak should differ when an authenticator actively authenticated the user (e.g. user entered the password), and when the user was authenticated passively (e.g. smart card authentication). IdPs should be considered too.
On active authentication, the auth_time will be set to current time. The passive authentication will leave auth_time unchanged and even unset (if not previously set).

Improve auth_time handling throughout Keycloak

h2. Why
Currently, the auth_time in Keycloak is handled incorrectly. Auth_time should be taken as the time the user entered the credentials, in other words when they actively participated in the authentication process. The current status is that Keycloak sets auth_time to current time in every auth flow except when the user is authenticated using SSO cookie.
*NOTE:* auth_time in this context is the [internal Keycloak variable| not necessarily the OIDC claim even though it's closely related.
h2. What
Reconsider how the auth_time is handled for all protocols and authenticators. Keycloak should differ when an authenticator actively authenticated the user (e.g. user entered the password), and when the user was authenticated passively (e.g. smart card authentication). IdPs should be considered too.
On active authentication, the auth_time will be set to current time. The passive authentication will leave auth_time unchanged and even unset (if not previously set).

summary: Not possible to create client in the admin console when client policy with "secure-redirecturi-enforce-executor" condition is used
description:
Steps to reproduce:
- Configure client policies in a way, that there is client policy applied for admin console client creation request, which points to the client profile with "secure-redirecturi-enforce-executor"
- Login as admin to the admin console and try to create client. It will fail due the "secure-redirecturi-enforce-executor" . Reason is, that the initial admin console screen for "create client" does not allow to specify things like "redirect URI" . Just the "root URL" of the client.
Possible improvement:
- In case that redirectUri on the client is not specified, just allow the request to pass (It should be fine as for the OIDC requests, it is needed that redirect URI exists. So the fact that client does not have "redirect_uri" should not be a security concern
- Not strictly needed to address the issue above, but optionally, we can improve this executor by add configuration option to check also other client URIs (not just the redirect URI) if they are "https" . Like web origin, root URL and admin URL.

summary: Client Policies : Revise SecureRequestObjectExecutor to have an option for checking "nbf" claim
description:
This ticket is the follow-up ticket for 
 Add "Verify Not-Before Claim" flag to "SecureRequestObjectExecutor".
If "ON", this executor check "nbf" as It has already done.
If "OFF", this executor do not check it.
The default value of this flag is "ON".
The former setting is needed to pass FAPI conformance test for FAPI 1.0 Advanced Final while the latter setting is needed to pass it for FAPI-RW ID2.

summary: Migration from Keycloak 13
description:
h2. Migration from Keycloak 13 (possibly check manually or in ClientPoliciesLoadUpdateTest)
Make sure that scenarios like this does not end with some strange exceptions:
 1) DB migration
 - Start Keycloak 13
 - Enable client policies
 - Configure some client profiles/policies as realm attributes
 - Migrate to latest Keycloak
 - Try to read the client profiles/policies saved in previous version
2) Export/import
 Similar scenario with export/import
I think it is ok if administrator needs to re-configure his client profiles and client policies (we may need to document it), but it is NOT ok if there is some exceptions and administrator is stucked entirely (with only workaround to delete the DB or manually remove the attributes of client policies/profiles from the realm)
h2. Test for migration from Keycloak 14
See details in the first comment below.

summary: Migration Client Registration Policies to Client Policies
description:
h2. What
This epic is about being able to fully migrate client registration policies to client policies. 
h2. How
The tasks needed to accomplish this might be:
- Makes sure that all Client Registration Policies Providers have corresponding executor/condition implementations available (Some of them have already available corresponding implementations in Keycloak 14 like TrustedHostClientRegistrationPolicy or ConsentRequiredClientRegistrationPolicy)
- Support for default client policies in newly created realms - see KEYCLOAK-18463
- Make sure Client Registration policies are removed and migrate them to client policies
- Make sure that Client Registration Policies are not referenced from any place in the Keycloak codebase, admin console or documentation
NOTE: Client Registration Policies are marked as deprecated in the Keycloak 14 documentation with note, that they might need to be replaced by client policies instead

summary: Support for default client policies in newly created realms
description:
h2. what
Makes sure that there is a mechanism, which will allow to have default client policies in newly created realms. This is currently not available for client policies (there are only "global client profiles" but not "global client policies"). It is needed as client registration policies have default registration policies defined in newly created realms. There is a need to either one of the options like:
- Auto-create client policies in newly created realms
- Have global client policies in each realm
- Have pre-defined default client policies in the "default" realm and makes them inherit in newly created child realms. This may depend on "Realm of realms" feature (Realms inheritance), which is not yet available in Keycloak 14
h2. why
This capability may be needed for being able to migrate Client Registration Policies to Client Policies. Because there are currently some auto-created Client Registration Policies in each realm after creation of new realm. There are some other tasks, which may require this feature.

summary: CIBA, support for additional parameters from the backchannel authentication request and backchannel authentication callback.
description:
The CIBA specification states in section 3:
{{This specification allows for some extensibility - profiles can be created that define additional parameters to be sent to, and received from, the Backchannel Authentication Endpoint.}}
With the purpose of increase the extensibility of the current implementation of CIBA, giving the option to use additional parameters in the protocol mappers, implement the following:

 * Add the support for additional parameters in the backchannel authentication callback parameters are inserted on the authentication session as notes with the prefix "ciba_callback_response_param_" to be used by protocol mappers.

summary: Cleanup ftl templates for all dynamic user profile related actions (register, update/verify profile, IDP review)
description:
As part of the configurable User Profile, we are working on dynamic templates for auth flow actions (KEYCLOAK-18428, KEYCLOAK-18429) and we should consider one more general change. I think now is the good time to change/clear this area as we are going to introduce new dynamic templates when configurable user profile is enabled, so there is not major impact on backward compatibility (old realms with legacy user profile will use old templates still)
Current state is that there are two "static" templates for these actions:
* {{register.ftl}} for registration form
* {{login-update-profile.ftl}} used for 'update profile' required action and for 'IDP review' - by my experience, this one mixes together two things which are a bit different (IDP review is more like new account registration) and is a bit hard to customize as context is not clearly available in it.
Both templates are very similar, {{register.ftl}} has password and re-captcha sections on top of update. By my experience from template customization for sso.redhat.com, customizing template means to do a lots of duplicate work in these two templates, and customizing {{login-update-profile.ftl}} is not easy due to its duality and not clear context info.
So I can see three possible ways where to go:
1. use only one template for all these action, with clear CONTEXT info available from freemarker context, so no duplicate code but customization per action still possible - IMHO this is the best option
2. keep two templates as is, add clear CONTEXT info into dynamic version of the login-update-profile.ftl to make it's customization a bit easier (this one will be also used for 'Verify profile' action automatically forced by user profile rules checks) - close to current state, but IMHO not a very good solution for template customization
3. create separate template for each action - solves problem with login-update-profile.ftl duality, but IMHO adds lots of duplicate code and maintenance work.
We have to discuss this change in community first to collect experience from other template customizers.

summary: Consistently record User profile attribute changes in UPDATE_PROFILE event
description:
We should consistently record User profile attribute changes in UPDATE_PROFILE event. It may be used as basic audit mechanism for user info changes.
Current status:
* UpdateProfile and VerifyProfile required actions record changes (old and new value) for email, firstName and lastName (in {{org.keycloak.authentication.requiredactions.UpdateProfile.processAction()}})
* update from old account console record changes (old and new value) for email, firstName and lastName (in {{org.keycloak.services.resources.account.AccountFormService.processAccountUpdate()}})
* update from new account console REST API doesn't record any change (in {{org.keycloak.services.resources.account.AccountRestService.updateAccount()}})
* IDP review fires this event when form is submitted, which is questionable at all as it is not update of the existing user (that event contains field "updated_email" even when it is not changed), this action also fires {{UPDATE_EMAIL}} event when email is changed from previous state.
Solution proposal:
* allow to configure in the UserProfile configuration which attribute change should be audited (tracked in this event)
* update places where event is fired to follow this configuration and add old and new value into event if tracked attribute is changed
* maybe the event should be updated inside of the UserProfile SPI provider to have consistent code? Or maybe we should use mechanism "UserAttributeProcessor SPI" which is just being discussed in the dev community.
* not sure what to do with the IDP review, at least add some info into event so it is visible where it comes from (probably we should add this into event from all places to see where the change happened)
Other notes:
* update from Admin REST API fires {{UPDATE}} admin event, it contains whole new user representation, but no any info about which attributes was really changed, maybe we shlould add this also
* {{UPDATE_EMAIL}} event doesn't look to be fired when email is changed from most of update places, not sure about its meaning of this event
* {{user.setEmailVerified(false)}} when email is changed is set only for old account console and required actions, not for new account console! Maybe this code should go inside of the UserProfile SPI provider to be consistent and in one place only.

summary: Introduce storage-independent ModelCriteria
description:
h2. Motivation
ModelCriteriaBuilder is currently built for individual map storages.
To be able to build the same criteria for multiple stores that are component of a tree storage, a storage-independent criteria is needed that can be then introspected by individual map storages and used as a template for building storage-specific criteria.
h2. What
1. Create storage-independent ModelCriteria which represents a Boolean expression built from predicates just as ModelCriteriaBuilder does now
2. Ensure that such a ModelCriteria is able to clone its expressions on arbitrary {{ModelCriteriaBuilder}}, thus replicate itself to an implementation-specific model criteria builder
3. This criteria builder should be able to convert itself to a String

summary: Do not force default to RS256 when verifying tokens sent by clients and JWK does not hold an algorithm
description:
The {{alg}} claim in a JWK is optional. 
Currently, if not set, Keycloak will default to {{RS256}} even though the client is configured with a specific algorithm for verifying signatures. Thus, causing signature verification to fail.
Instead, if {{alg}} is not available from JWK, Keycloak should take into account the algorithm set for the context where signature verification is happening (e.g.: request object, JWT client auth, etc).

summary: Configurable OIDC WellKnown provider
description:
h2. What
It may be good to have more flexibility around default implementation of OIDC WellKnown provider. This may be needed for OpenBanking Brazil, but also for other use-cases.
h2. Requirements
- Ability to override some claims (EG. "claims_supported" or "scopes_supported"). Or possibly all claims. Either add new values or limit existing values in these claims. Especially there should be an ability to filter some scopes, which are provided by default
- Ability to add new claims (EG. see KEYCLOAK-18636 for the details)
- [OPTIONAL] ability to add new claims or change the claims without a need to change the implementation of OIDC WellKnown provider. This will be good for better extensibility, so that when some new OAuth/OIDC/FAPI related RFC is needed to be supported by KEycloak, people don't need to change the code inside OIDC WellKnown provider, but they can isolate their code inside separate package. This requirement could mean that we may need separate SPI like "OIDCWellKnownProviderCustomizer", which will be basically interceptor to change some claims inside WellKnown endpoint ?
- [OPTIONAL] Possibility to override default provider with the ID "openid-configuration" id. OIDC specification specifies that OIDC WellKnown provider mist be available under <<issuer>>/.well-known/openid-configuration , which means in the case something like . The suffix /.well-known/openid-configuration is mandatory and hence it cannot be something like . At least in the Wildfly, this is already possible as when you create your own WellKnown provider with ID "openid-configuration" and deploy it in some module, it will take precedence over the default provider.

summary: Support cert-bound tokens when doing client credentials grant
description:
Currently, we only support cert-bound tokens when using code flow.
For FAPI, it is also important to bound tokens with certificates when using MTLS and the client credentials grant.
A driven use case is clients obtaining tokens on their behalf to access OpenBanking APIs like consent and resources.
full_text:
Support cert-bound tokens when doing client credentials grant

Currently, we only support cert-bound tokens when using code flow.
For FAPI, it is also important to bound tokens with certificates when using MTLS and the client credentials grant.

description:
*Motivation:*
Keycloak does not support automatic update SAML/OIDC IdP metadata. Admin can only import IdP from metadata url. Automatic update will make ongoing maintenance easier.
*Proposal:* 
Implementation is based on Hynek comment for SAML/OIDC IdP in the main issue :
|What would be needed is the following: * Store with the clients in the attributes: What IdP (if any) it comes from; Whether metadata refresh is enabled flag
 * Store with the identity provider: Metadata URL, Last refresh time, Refresh period; Whether to delete clients which are not found in metadata flag; Whether to add clients that are found in the metadata and do not exist
 * Scheduler that would periodically find identity providers that are past refresh time, then find those clients that should be updated and update those
 * Support for SAML and OIDC metadata format|
 admin can select to autoupdate metadata when creating a SAML/OIDC IdP (autoupdate field by default to false). When autoupdate is true, realm admin must fulfill Refresh period field( default 1 day).
For SAML Identity Provider, realm admin must fulfill Metadata URL.
For OIDC Identity Provider, realm admin must fulfill Issuer. Metadata URL automatically become equal to issuer + '/.well-known/openid-configuration'.
Although Realm Admin can update all SAML/OIDC IdP fields, SAML/OIDC IdP fields imported from metadata will be updated during autoupdate. Realm Admin can select/ deselect autoupdate metadata during SAML/OIDC IdP update.
For each automated SAML/OIDC IdP a scheduler that refreshes IdP metadata every refresh period will be created. Every time Keycloak starts, schedulers for autoupdates IdPs will be created.

summary: Create implementations automatically from an interface: Map*EntityImpl
description:
Currently, Map*Entity implementation is maintained by a developer, so changes in the interface need to be manually propagated to the implementation. This increases maintenance cost and is also error-prone due to the need to update the {{isUpdated}} method.
Create a map-based implementation of the Map*Entity interface based on an interface that would be generated automatically using javac annotation processing.

summary: Should not issue tokens if the request doesn't meet the security profile.
description:
When I created a client policy which have a "client-roles" type condition and a "fapi-1-advanced" profile and created the specified client role at the client's role settings, the following tokens were issued with no error.
- Not sender-constraint. This is because "OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens Enabled" was OFF.
- Signed with RS256. This is because "Access Token Signature Algorithm" and "ID Token Signature Algorithm" were not specified.
- "redirect_uri" is not checked. This is because "Valid Redirect URIs" was "*".
I think it's good that we are not forced to change the client settings to be suitable for each security profile.
This is because one of the client policy's purposes is avoiding the over 40 settings for those security profiles.
It's OK if the client acts suitable for the selected security profile no matter what the client settings are.
But it's NG if the client acts not suitable for the selected security profile (like the above) with no error.

summary: Separate arquillian framework and abstract tests from base testsuite
description:
Current state:
{noformat}
- testsuite:
 - integration-arquillian:
 - servers: ...
 - tests:
  - base
  - other:
  - adapters
  - admin-ui
  - mod-auth-mellon
  - ...
{noformat}
The problem is that the {{other/*}} test modules depend on the {{base}} module for common classes and test-classes while the {{base}} module also contains its own tests. This means it needs to be built twice: once with {{-DskipTests}} before the other modules can run, and once to run it's own tests.
Solution would be to move the common classes (arq. extensions, page objects, utils, etc) and the *abstract* test classes to a separate "framework" module and remove dependency of the other modules on the {{base}} module:
{noformat}
- testsuite:
 - integration-arquillian:
 - framework
 - servers: ...
 - tests:
  - base
  - adapters
  - admin-ui
  - mod-auth-mellon
  - ...
{noformat}

summary: MSAD Password policy tests
description:
It will be good to have a test for scenarios like:
- Register new user with weak password and ensure that he is required to update password right after registration (He has UPDATE_PASSWORD requiredAction set on him). This is already done in LDAPMSADMapperTest.test01RegisterUserWithWeakPasswordFirst , however test is currently skiped
- Test for passwordHistory scenarios (eg. user can't update his password through account management or through UPDATE_PASSWORD requiredAction to some old password. But admin can still update it).
- Test that admin or user can't set weak password
Those tests will require a way to set the password policy on MSAD server. The passwordPolicy attributes (maxPwdAge, minPwdAge, minPwdLength, pwdHistoryLength, pwdProperties) can be set on LDAP side at the DC record, but then it is set for the whole MSAD domain, which can clash with the other projects using MSAD server. There are likely other ways to set the password policies on MSAD side. 
We need to figure a good way to set the password policies on MSAD side. This can be either:
- Ensure that some MSAD domain is dedicated just for the Keycloak test (this is easily doable if we will test just with our own MSAD virtual machines)
- Figure other way to set the password policied, which won't clash with the setup by other people.
full_text:
MSAD Password policy tests

It will be good to have a test for scenarios like:
- Register new user with weak password and ensure that he is required to update password right after registration (He has UPDATE_PASSWORD requiredAction set on him). This is already done in LDAPMSADMapperTest.test01RegisterUserWithWeakPasswordFirst , however test is currently skiped
- Test for passwordHistory scenarios (eg. user can't update his password through account management or through UPDATE_PASSWORD requiredAction to some old password. But admin can still update it).
- Test that admin or user can't set weak password
Those tests will require a way to set the password policy on MSAD server. The passwordPolicy attributes (maxPwdAge, minPwdAge, minPwdLength, pwdHistoryLength, pwdProperties) can be set on LDAP side at the DC record, but then it is set for the whole MSAD domain, which can clash with the other projects using MSAD server. There are likely other ways to set the password policies on MSAD side. 
We need to figure a good way to set the password policies on MSAD side. This can be either:
- Ensure that some MSAD domain is dedicated just for the Keycloak test (this is easily doable if we will test just with our own MSAD virtual machines)
- Figure other way to set the password policied, which won't clash with the setup by other people.

summary: Use HS256 for refresh tokens
description:
Currently we sign refresh tokens with RSA. We can probably save some performance points by using HMAC for refresh tokens instead, since it's the Keycloak itself which signs and verifies it and from the adapter perspective, refresh token is just an opaque string.
We should just make sure that when this is changed, offline tokens migrated from previous versions will still work. We can probably support both RSA and HMAC for verifying tokens and decide based on the JWT header.

summary: Invalidate existing user sessions at logon
description:
Currently a user can log into multiple client application sessions across many devices. 
This may lead the user to believe that any existing sessions are no longer active as credentials are required each time whilst any previous sessions remain open for the duration of the access token. This is especially true if the user does not complete a system logoff, i.e. would simply close down a web browser.
It would be useful to be able to secure the system further by providing a Realm or Client level configuration option to *Invalidate Existing User Sessions at Logon*

summary: Possible loadbalancer optimizations
description:
With KEYCLOAK-4626 we have StickySessionEncoderProvider, which abstracts how the sticky session information added to the request. By default it is adding the routeId to the AUTH_SESSION_ID cookie similarly like Wildfly is doing for http sessions.
It seems we should doublecheck the behaviour of the most popular loadbalancers and then check if we can/should add some optimizations. What we likely should do is:
- Have the implementation of StickySessionEncoderProvider, which won't do anything. It will be solely responsibility of loadbalancer to somehow add the session stickiness or eventually don't use sticky sessions at all
- Optionally look if some optimizations can be done for backchannel requests (code-token, refresh token, backchannel logouts etc)

summary: Remove roles, protocolMappers, timestamp from AuthenticatedClientSessionModel
description:
The protocolMappers and roles need to be removed from AuthenticatedClientSessionModel. They are currently here because of:
- Scope parameter. There might be different roles, protocolMappers based on the used scope parameter
- Consent : We want to ensure that same roles+protocolMappers approved on consent screen are used in clientSession and not any others
There might be an issue here, because right now, we have just single AuthenticatedClientSessionModel per client+userSession . So we rather need to move roles+protocolMappers to code JWT and refreshToken JWT, which will ensure that multiple clientSessions of same userSession may have different roles+protocolMappers according to scope etc.
There are other things, which likely should be removed from AuthenticatedClientSessionModel. At least timestamp and possibly some other things. Eventually we need to doublecheck if it's possible to remove AuthenticatedClientSessionModel entirely and have userSession to contain just list of client UUIDs.

summary: Ensure code-to-token flow works in concurrent SSO login to same client
description:
Right now, code is saved as a note in AuthenticatedClientSessionModel before AuthorizationRequest is redirected to the application and this note is then compared once code-to-token request is received from the application.
There are issues with concurrent SSO login of same client now (case when user has multiple browser tabs and opens concurrently at the same time). This should be improved. Rather we need to have the code as JWT and the list of expired codes.
Test: ConcurrentLoginTest and ConcurrentLoginClusterTest should work even if it uses same clients in all threads (Right now, each thread need to have separate set of clients to have test passing)

summary: Tuning of JDG communication
description:
We will try to ensure at Keycloak level that there are not unecessary communication between JDG servers.
Some improvements can be done in the lower level.
- There is TODO in InfinispanNotificationsManager.hotrodEventReceived . The value of event need to be separately retrieved from the JDG, which is unecessary overhead.
- Check if events can be grouped together as much as possible. Something can be done in infinispan/jgroups configuration level, but maybe we have some low-hanging fruit to be done on our side too (eg. ensure that invalidation events are sent in list instead of each event sent in separate message etc)
- Tune at JDG level: We can possibly add converterFilters or converterFactories as described in JDG documentation. It will require custom code on JDG side, but hopefully it won't need to have dependencies on Keycloak server classes. It may require that every event will contain the sender site (and maybe also sender node), so that it's possible to skip calling ClientListeners for the events, which were sent by the particular Keycloak node itself (or which were sent from the other node from our own DC).

summary: NPE and endless browser loop in security admin console if client access type is changed to "confidential"
description:
*Observed behaviour*
* Browser gets into an endless loop logging into the admin console
*Expected behavior*
* User logs into the admin console as normal
*Analysis*
* In AdminConsole.java:180 a new ClientManager is created using a parameterless constructor (not passing a RealmManager)
* After calling ClientManager.toInstallationRepresentation(...), an NPE is thrown in ClientManager.java:355 since no RealmManager is set
* This path is only taken if the client is not a public client (see ClientManager.java:294) which the security admin console normally is not
*Proposed fix*
* Create a RealmManager and pass it to new ClientManager(...) in AdminConsole.config() similar to AdminConsole.whoAmI()
I rated this only minor as it was just me messing with the default config so I don't think it is really critical. On the other hand, it is easy to fix and hard to get out of the situation if you made the wrong change (but so is removing the admin role from yourself as I did. :) )

summary: Optimize front-channel logout - Via IFRAME
description:
Derived from KEYCLOAK-4899.
{quote}
The algorithm in AuthenticationManager.browserLogout works in a way that:
- It finds the userSession and tracks all the clients supporting backchannel logout. The Logout request is sent to them
- For the frontchannel logout, which is currently supported just for SAML, there is a chain of browser redirects . The particular client redirects back to keycloak after doing it's logout and then Keycloak redirects to other frontchannel client. Keycloak tracks, which client needs to be logged-out through the update on userSession. So currently when there is userSession with N fronchannel clients, there are N+1 updates to the userSession during logout before userSession is finally removed.
\[[~mposolda@redhat.com]\] thinks that for cross-dc, we may optimize to have just 1 write to userSession. We can improve this by:
- Using iframes for the frontchannel logout. There is some discussion on ML [1] . Using iframes has some other advantages and generally it's much better and more robust than browser redirects approach.
[1] 
{quote}
This feature is almost complete and involves fixing a TODO in [this branch| in [this commit|
* 
This would most likely lead to a parameter of client that would define allowed origins to be allowed to load from within IFRAME as set by Content-Security-Policy.
Note that currently the frontchannel logout is only supported by SAML clients.

description:
This JIRA is to track user interest in making authentication sessions replicated across sites in cross-DC settings. If you are interested in this functionality, vote for this issue.
Since currently the authentication sessions are not replicated across sites, for certain operations sticky sessions are necessary to makes sure that related requests end up in the same site.

summary: Context accessibility for JS base policies
description:
Considering that resources might be created specifying a variable (i.e /myendpoint/{var}). It would be of great help to be able to retrieve this "var" value in the $evaluation.context in order to test it and grant/deny access dynamically on such criteria. 
In the same idea, considering that it isn't rare to have the exact same resource in an API that just gets accessed with a different HTTP verb, retrieving the http method in the context would also be useful.

# After the test finishes, compare the counts in database tables in the individual nodes. They should match

summary: Ensure that RefreshToken doesn't need to send request to the other DC
description:
Currently it's already mechanism to ensure that LastSessionRefreshes are send to the other DC periodically in "batches", so that there is no need to send cross-dc message between DCs for every refreshToken request.
In some cases, there is still the message sent immediately to the other DC (For example when refreshToken request comes in time 29:59 and idle timeout is 30 minutes, it's send immediately because otherwise the other DC will receive update later for example in time 31:04 (assuming 5 seconds for sending the message between DC). It will be a window when it will treat the correct refreshToken as incorrect). We want to always skip that and instead allow some window when refreshTokens will be still allowed (EG. refreshToken will be allowed in idleTimeout+2 minutes. IdleTimeout periodic cleaner thread will use idleTimeout+4 minutes).
The only exception will be the case with "revokeRefreshToken", which will still send requests immediately for now.
full_text:

summary: Create a mapper for adding a received claim value to the users session notes
description:
In a broker situation, the Keycloak broker may want to store a claim value received from the IDP in the users session notes, to support the content of claims in the tokens issued by the broker.
Specifically, if the IDP returns a given acr value as a claim in the access token, this acr value should be used in the access token issued by the broker. Populating the access token can be done using the UserSessionNoteMapper.

This whould also help when implementing a stepwise stress testing loop, which increments the number of users in each iteration and checks the assertions if system performance is still acceptable.

description:
Provide a stress-testing option in the performance testsuite.
A stress test is a performance test in which the load is being gradually increased until the system starts performing bad. The main goal is _to find the performance limits_ which can usually be expressed as:
- _a maximum number of users_ which the system can service in a satisfactory way (acceptable response time, etc.), or
- _a maximum achieved request throughput_.
The load can be ramped up linearly, or in a series of intervals with steady load.

summary: Enhance Keycloak Web Admin Console Design to Support Scalability
description:
As current Admin Console design, there will be one client to be created for each other realm other than master during the admin console loading time.
When there is lot's of realms created since last admin console loaded, then there will be lot's of clients to be created in master realm by the API of _/auth/admin/master/console/whoami_, which will take considerable time to load the UI.
Even after the whoami API is loaded, there will be a _/auth/admin/realms
_ request almost after every user interaction in the UI. 
Let's say that when there will be 1K realms in database, these batch data fetch would be not acceptable for the Admin UI data change.
Proposed Design for Web Admin Console
1. Web Admin Console access should just based on the admin user access token, not the 
2. API _/auth/admin/realms
_ should be designed by Pagination base, and this API may also be only trigered once user reach to the page: `auth/admin/master/console/#/realms`, and this web page would also need to support pagination.
3. API _/auth/admin/master/console/whoami_ should be desgined for per request per realm
4. We may not need to create clients like 'xxx-realm' in master realm

* Add ability to specify if an event listener should join the transaction or not. If joining the event will be sent just prior to committing the transaction. If not joining the event the event will be sent just after committing the transaction.

* Consider adding specific listeners for example UserEventListener (user created, user updated, user deleted), AuthenticationEventListener (login success, login failed)
* Add ability to receive event before/after

summary: Open workload injection model
description:
In our performance tests, we currently use a "closed" workload injection model* which is characterized by a constant number of active users. The arrival rate of new users is dynamically adapted to system's performance because a new user only arrives when one of the active users finishes the scenario.
We should consider moving to an "open" injection model which is characterized by user arrival rate independent on system performance, for example using Gatling's {{constantUsersPerSec(rate)}} construct.
Advantages:
- more realistic workload
Disadvantages:
- It seems to be more difficult to find the exact value of arrival rate which can put enough pressure on the system and not trigger a "runaway" process where the number of active users steadily increases during the test.
*)

summary: Common approach to writing performance tests
description:
Currently we have 2 performance test cases each written in a different style:
- {{DeaultSimulation}} (implementing an OIDC login-refresh-logout scenario) includes a detailed description of test scenario.
- {{AdminConsoleSimulation}} hides most details in a common {{SimulationHelper}} class and as a result it seems to be more readable. However due to Gatling limitations all common code would have to be put in this one helper class in the furure which doesn't seem very modular and maintainable.
We should decide which one of these approaches to take, or find out if there is some other alternative. We should also put a short note/guideline in the readme.

summary: Investigate upper limits of amount on userSessions
description:
Will be good to be able to test performance with big number of userSessions. Also assuming that every of them will have configurable number of clientSessions (1-5 but that's not a priority).
Especially will be nice to test it with cluster and test:
- Some normal events like:
-- login/logout user
-- Showing tab "sessions" from account management
- Some admin events like:
-- Tab "sessions" is displayed for particular realm, client or user
-- Realm/client/user is removed
-- Periodic expiration of userSessions is triggered (maybe it's sufficient to have a test, which will manually trigger "UserSessionProvider.removeExpired" 
It's especially important to test that in cluster (and optionally verify that network communication between cluster nodes is not that big). In past, we had issues like for example showing tab "sessions" will block admin console and make Keycloak unusable (due the fact that with million of sessions, it was trying to download 500K userSessions from the other cluster node).

summary: Test performance of IdentityProvider use-cases
description:
Test things like:
- Identity provider login
- Identity provider linking in account management
- Various configuration for identity Provider. For example, in past we had bad performance when OIDC Identity Provider was configured with "Verify signatures" (due the fact that Keycloak always decoded and created PublicKey to verify signature of identityProvider from the PEM string, which itself is quite CPU time consuming). And similar for SAML.

summary: Audience support for Client Scopes
description:
Few things how it can work:
- We will have protocolMapper implementation, which will be able to add specified clientId to the audience claim inside token. The audience value won't be limited just to the clients (for example, some vendors may expect URL as a value of audience)
- It is possible to automatically generate new client scope "foo-service" based on the service client (typically bearer-only client) "foo-service". By default, the client scope contains:
-- Audience protocol mapper with clientId of client "foo-service"
-- All client roles of the bearer-only client "foo-service"
- Frontend client can easily add the "foo-service" scope to his "Default Scopes" or "Optional Scopes" . It means that "foo-service" will be added to the audience inside access token and client will be allowed to have Role Scope Mappings of all roles of "foo-service" bearer-only client.
- If more flexibility is needed, admin can easily change the default (EG. Client Scope "foo-service" can be divided into 2 scopes, when each of them will contain just some subset of roles (EG. "foo read-only scope" , "foo read /write scope" ).
- Adapter support for audience - Will be done in the followup JIRA KEYCLOAK-3058 . It will be possibly some flag in the keycloak.json whether audience should be verified and will need to be false by default (due the backwards compatibility)

kind: ClusterServiceBroker
metadata:
 name: BestCompanySaaS
spec:
 url: 
 authInfo:
 basic:
 secretRef:

 name: secret-name
{noformat}

description:
Create something that approximates what PNC maven builds do during productisation. This is intended so that the pipeline can execute completely even if there's some sort of problem with actual PNC (lack of credentials, random bugs, etc.)
What I think might work for this is to start with an empty local maven repo, and then execute the series of maven builds (including PME), then zip up the local repo as the maven repository zip deliverable. Generally the pipeline can also access the local repo for any artifacts it might download from PNC normally.
Generally the artifacts that are produced should have the correct product version number (ex: 7.2.1), but don't have to use the proper productised dependencies, as we'd never ship anything from this simulator.

summary: [SPIKE] - Improvements to RESTful Security
description:
This spike is about improvements to authorization services in order to better support RESTful security.
As an outcome we should be able to identify:
* Improvements to PEP and PDP in order to allow resource servers to push arbitrary claims to policies.
* Improvements to PEP in order to allow users to listen for specific authorization events fired during processing of requests.
* PEP configuration options we are missing in order to control PEP behavior. For instance, caching of path configurations, loading of resources.

summary: [SPIKE] Pipeline: How to deal with number of matrix jobs
description:
The matrix jobs are not common part of the pipeline definitions. 
In the issue [KEYCLOAK-6533| there is described how we can generate a matrix jobs but two generated matrixes was executed in sequence. The purpose of this task is to try several parallel matrix jobs, how we can generate them and we can do some logical/visual split between the matrixes. The second part of the task is to generate the same number of stages based on the all jobs/matrixes useally executed in the parent jobs.
*Acceptance criteria*
* PoC of the pipeline definitions for more parallel matrixes
* Description how we can visually split the matrixes (is possible)
* PoC of the pipeline with the same number of the stages as in the keycloak parent job (including all matrixes/combinations)

summary: [SPIKE] How do we do a flow with the logs.
description:

Current setup:
* Bot runs the jenkins job
** automatically when the owner of the PR is in the dev group
** manually - when asked by someone from dev group
* The pipeline (jenkins job)
** builds the master with PR
** runs the tests
** send the status of the PR (FAILED/SUCCESS) back to GitHub
*Acceptance criteria*
* Description or flow diagram of the design
* The design should answer following questions:
** Who will be responsible for storing and filtering the logs. Jenkins? Bot?
** Jenkins pipeline currently reports the status of the build to GitHub. Should we change that behaviour?

summary: [RH-SSO] Refactor existing application templates for RH-SSO for OpenShift image to dynamically create necessary Java keystores/truststores in OpenShift
description:
Currently [available application templates for RH-SSO for OpenShift image| expect the user to provide definition of:
* SSL keystore,
* JGroups keystore, and
* SSL truststore
in order the TLS (https) configuration for the image to work correctly. Since the SSL keystore / truststore and JGroups keystore configuration is not trivial, it creates initial barrier for image adoption / use.
To lower this initial barrier, the RH-SSO application templates should be refactored to:
* Utilize the OpenShift's internal / integral [serving certificate secrets service| functionality to generate the TLS certificate / key pair automatically,
* Utilize [re-encrypt| TLS mode / route type instead the current [passthrough | one,
* Use the OpenShift's [init containers| functionality to convert the previously generated PEM format based TLS certificate/key pair into PKCS12 format, and dynamically create necessary Java keystore/truststore from these.

summary: public clients can only exchange refresh token
description: It is possible for an untrusted service to exchange a bearer token it receive from a public client for any target the client is allowed to exchange for. To prevent this, only allow public clients to change a refresh token for another token type. The fact that a public client has a refresh token means it successfully participated in an oauth authentication flow and that there is at least some trust that the public client asking for a token exchange is who it says it is.
full_text:
public clients can only exchange refresh token

It is possible for an untrusted service to exchange a bearer token it receive from a public client for any target the client is allowed to exchange for. To prevent this, only allow public clients to change a refresh token for another token type. The fact that a public client has a refresh token means it successfully participated in an oauth authentication flow and that there is at least some trust that the public client asking for a token exchange is who it says it is.

description:
Currently the WildFly adapter (and others) store the tokens in the users HTTP session. 
As long as the application is stateful and already uses sessions there's no problem with that. However, for applications that has been designed to be stateless (clustered without sticky sessions) that can be problematic.
We should add an option to the adapters to have them store the tokens in cookies instead of the HTTP session.
full_text:
Stateless support for adapters

Currently the WildFly adapter (and others) store the tokens in the users HTTP session. 
As long as the application is stateful and already uses sessions there's no problem with that. However, for applications that has been designed to be stateless (clustered without sticky sessions) that can be problematic.
We should add an option to the adapters to have them store the tokens in cookies instead of the HTTP session.

summary: Log out only non-offline sessions in admin console and account console
description:
When the realm admin endpoint {{/logout-all}} is invoked, possibly from the admin GUI, a not before policy is also set to the realm. This causes not only user sessions to be invalidated, but also any existing offline sessions.
Based upon how the Logout All action is shown in the admin GUI Sessions tab, it is hard to tell that this is the intended behavior since the Sessions tab lists active sessions excluding offline sessions together with the Logout All action.
If a not before policy is supposed to be set and pushed, there is separate functionality to do so.

summary: UMA permissions not considered when asking for user entitlements
description:
My set-up is a follows:
1. I have a policy that says that the owner of a resource is authorised with scope read, write and delete. Such policy is attached to a resource with a * path (e.g. /resource/*).
2. User A create a resource /resource/A
3. User A ask all permissions. He is returned he can do anything on /resource/A
So far so good. Now it's the part that i believe is not working as i would expect.
4. User B create a resource /resource/B
5. User B share resource B with User A
6. User A ask all permissions. He is returned he can do anything on /resource/A but no information is returned about resource B,
 despite there is a permission granted.
It looks like User A can check if he can access resource B only if I create a permission ticket and I specifically check that, but as a requester,
I don't know in advance if i am authorised to access a resource via UMA ticket or via another policy.
In fact, if ask if i have read permission using the permission parameter, i get not authorised:
curl --request POST \
 --url \
 --header 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \
 --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
 --data 'grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Auma-ticket&permission=da2fdbf6-076e-4716-8b91-2c7feeda8bee%23read&audience=test'
while if i create a ticket for that resource with permission read, i get authorised.

summary: Support Policy Management in Protection API
description:
As a developer, I want to manage permissions for resources protected by Keycloak using a single endpoint so that I can easily manage the policies that govern access to these resources.
Currently, policy management is possible using Keycloak Admin REST API, which provides a fine-grained API for each policy type we support. However, that requires from developers interacting with multiple endpoints instead of a single endpoint with a unified contract that hides complexity and the different policy representations, making easier to manage policies, especially user-defined policies (UMA).

However, that requires from developers interacting with multiple endpoints instead of a single endpoint with a unified contract that hides complexity and the different policy representations, making easier to manage policies, especially user-defined policies (UMA).

summary: User-Managed Policy Provider
description:
This is about refactoring UMA support to manage user managed permissions (e.g.: permissions granted directly by the user so others can access their resources) just like any other permission we have in Keycloak.
We should be able to:
* Support a specific Policy Provider for UMA Permissions
* Create UMA Permissions when a ticket is granted
* Remove UMA Permissions when a ticket is revoked
* Query policies managed by the user
Currently, we evaluate UMA permissions by checking whether or not permission tickets were granted.

description:
It will be useful to have configuration option on adapters like "always-refresh-token" . When this option is true, then adapter will send request for refreshing accessToken during each request (doesn't apply for bearer authentication). 
This might be handy as for some setups like:
- applications, which have token in cookie - KEYCLOAK-702
- non-distributable applications in cluster
it is no other reliable way to propagate logout event.

summary: Cross-dc openshift: make sure that Keycloak can handle restart of JDG and moving to different IP addres
description:
During summit demo, we often saw the following issue:
- Keycloak was configured for cross-dc setup and was dependent on JDG server, which was deployed on same Openshif cloud in different project (namespace).
- JDG was available to Keycloak under some well-known service name and port EG. jdg-app-hotrod.datagrid.svc:11222
- In case that JDG was re-deployed and JDG service was moved to other IP (EG. previously jdg-app-hotrod.datagrid.svc was on IP 1.2.3.4, but after JDG re-deploy it was moved to 5.6.7.8 ), the Keycloak wasn't able to adapt to that and was still trying to connect to old IP -> FAIL
Possibilities to address: 
- Wait until we upgrade to wildfly 13 where are WFLY-10269 and ISPN-7955 addressed
- Maybe improve the liveness probe in the RHSSO Openshift image (add some healthcheck and periodically call it to detect if RHSSO is able to connect to JDG. If it's not, then RHSSO pod should be restarted. This was workaround done in summit demo - KEYCLOAK-7186 .
I think we should do both things together to improve on such scenario.

summary: cluster-aware logout for non-distributable applications
description:
When single-sign-out is triggered by Keycloak server for distributable apps, the logout event can be send to any cluster node where particular distributable app is deployed. Since sessions are replicated, the invalidation, which will happen on this host, will be propagated to all other cluster hosts.
For non-distributable apps it is more tricky. To handle it, there will be mechanism like:
- Application will send in codeToToken it's hostname during login. This hostname is then send in ClientSession on Keycloak
- Once logout is triggered, Keycloak will be able to find the hostname from the clientSession and send logout event to particular host
Application, which want to use this mechanism will use adminUrl like:
{code}
{code}
In this case ${kc_session_host} will be dynamically replaced with the hostname from ClientSession. For apps, which don't use adminUrl like this, there will be single logout event sent as is now.

summary: Check using HotRodStore instead of RemoteStore
description:
Wildfly 13 has HotRodStore together with RemoteStore (which may be deprecated). 
It's possible that HotRodStore would be better choice than RemoteStore, but will be good to wait first until it's more mature. HotRodStore among other things, means:
- Easier configuration (there is single shared configuration of RemoteCache Manager without need to duplicate configurations related to RemoteCache settings)
- Better performance and sharing resources - RemoteStore uses RemoteCache with it's own RemoteCacheManager, so for 7 caches with 7 RemoteStores, we have 7 separate RemoteCacheManager. This means wasting of resources (pools etc). With HotRodStore, we will have just 1 RemoteCacheManager (hopefully).
- RemoteStore may be deprecated and won't support newer things available by HotRodStore (EG SSL, Authentication etc)
Disadvantages:
- HotRodStore is dependency of Wildfly/EAP itself (not Infinispan). Likely not possible to easily use with Keycloak-on-embedded-undertow

7.3.0.CD02-redhat-1

summary: Ensure that infinispan session entities are owned by local node
description:
Currently we have some support for sticky session added with the cookie AUTH_SESSION_ID. 
In cluster environment, we try to update the route of the session always when the owner of the particular session is changing in a similar way like Wildfly is doing for Http Sessions (JSESSIONID cookie).
So for the optimal performance, it is required that loadbalancer is configured to use AUTH_SESSION_ID as sticky session and it will let the backend server (Keycloak) to manage routes.
Problem is, that in many cases, administrators don't have a possibility to update the loadbalancer configuration. So as a best-effort, we may try to be more optimal out-of-the-box in case that admins can't tweak loadbalancer configuration. What we can possibly do is:
- Use Infinispan KeyAffinityService and always ensure that current node where the HTTP request is processed (creator of AuthenticationSession) will generate the AUTH_SESSION_ID owned by himself. This will ensure that loadbalancers, which automatically use current node as a route, will really route to the owner node. (Note that this configuration is still not super-optimal as in case of cluster re-balance, the owner may be changed but route won't be updated)
- Use infinispan Grouping API for client sessions and use the userSessionId as the group ID. So clientSessions will be saved on same node as their corresponding user session. 
There is also still possibility to merge clientSessions back to userSession (we may need to doublecheck performance of this and maybe do some research how many client sessions typical user session has in production environments).

Problem is, that in many cases, administrators don't have a possibility to update the loadbalancer configuration. So as a best-effort, we may try to be more optimal out-of-the-box in case that admins can't tweak loadbalancer configuration. What we can possibly do is:
- Use Infinispan KeyAffinityService and always ensure that current node where the HTTP request is processed (creator of AuthenticationSession) will generate the AUTH_SESSION_ID owned by himself. This will ensure that loadbalancers, which automatically use current node as a route, will really route to the owner node. (Note that this configuration is still not super-optimal as in case of cluster re-balance, the owner may be changed but route won't be updated)
- Use infinispan Grouping API for client sessions and use the userSessionId as the group ID. So clientSessions will be saved on same node as their corresponding user session.

summary: Add X509 configuration for the openshift image
description:
The openshift image needs to be customized (standalone-openshift.xml) in order to use the X509 / Certificate login. X509 login needs the configuration of the HTTPS realm (keystore and trust-store) and setting the verify-client option to REQUESTED (see [documentation|
In the openshift image the trust-store in the ApplicationRealm cannot be configured (only the ssl server-identity is set):
{code:xml}
<security-realm name="ApplicationRealm">
 ...
 <authentication>
 ... 
 <truststore path="cacerts" relative-to="jboss.server.config.dir" keystore-password="XXXX"/>
 </authentication>
</security-realm>
{code}
And the verify-client option in the undertow https connector cannot be set either:
{code:xml}
<https-listener name="https" socket-binding="https" security-realm="ApplicationRealm" verify-client="REQUESTED"/>
{code}

summary: Vertical nav bar testability
description:
Currently, there's no way to properly test the vertical nav bar (on the left) as there's no "nice" way of selecting its items - they have no ID attributes.
We can't select them by index since the nav bar is dynamic and its content's based on various Realm settings.
We'd like to avoid using the visible text for selection as this causes stability issues in some browsers. Also, this way we'd bound the test to specific localization string.
We can't use selecting by "href" attribute either. The test should check if the button leads to a correct page. Using the link itself to select the button wouldn't tell us much.
Ideally we need to add some unique IDs to the nav items. But this is no easy task since the whole nav bar is generated by PatternFly-ng.
