- It is still in draft state for few years and there are some TODO in
it. So hard to say how much to rely on it...
- It specifically talks about "scope" parameter and mentions, that it is
often used by various parties for "what the token can be used for"
(permissions/claims associated with the token) and "where to use that
token" . But it mentions that "where" use-case should be ideally handled
by something else.
- It introduces "resource" parameter, which MUST be an absolute URI per
this specification and it should point to the service/resource where the
access token will be used. When authorization server is creating token,
it may apply audiences, encrypt token by various algorithms based on the
requested "resource" etc. For the audience, they specify that:
"The authorization server may use the exact 'resource' value as the
audience or it may map from that value to a more general URI or abstract
identifier for the resource server."
- The "resource" parameter is used in the token request if possible. For
the grants where it's not possible (implicit, resource owner password
login, client credentials) it is used in the initial authentication
request. So for the classic "authorization_code" grant it can be used in
code-to-token or refresh-token requests. This is great and allows some
cool flexibility (unlike "scope" where the whole SSO login including all
the redirects is needed). But it requires some support on adapters.
For support of this specs, we can maybe have the option to drive audiences through both "scope" and "resource" params.
The "resource" related support will require changes on the adapter side
as it is new parameter to be supported in code-to-token request and
refresh-token request. On our adapter's side, it will be good to have
some changes to allow "cache" of more access tokens for various
resources/audiences, not just one. On server-side, I was thinking about
various possibilities, and it still looks good to represent "resource"
support through client scopes. So optional clientScopes can be requested
either through "scope" parameter (default case) or through "resource"
parameter (probably disabled by default) or through both. I think we can support "resource" to be clientId, not just an URL. And support more "resource" parameters, so that accessToken can have more audiences (The specs has TODO on this at the time of this writing).

summary: Default OIDC clientScope for add roles and audience to the access token
description:
- Add support for priorities to ProtocolMapperModel
- Add new client scope "oidc-default", which will be added as default client scope to the realms and to all the existing clients (during migration)
- Add 2 protocol mappers to this "oidc-default" client scope:
- OIDCRolesProtocolMapper - the new protocol mapper, which will add roles to the access token instead of adding them automatically as we do now - 
- AudienceClientRolesProtocolMapper - the new protocol mapper, which will add audience to the access token for all the clients, which has any client roles in the token. Need to have lower priority than the OIDCRolesProtocolMapper
- I would still add the "realm-management" client scope, but not add it to any clients. In the docs, we can recommend people to not use "Full Scope Allowed" (which we already do) and use "scope=realm-management" just if they want to call admin REST API with their token.

Default OIDC clientScope for add roles and audience to the access token

- Add support for priorities to ProtocolMapperModel
- Add new client scope "oidc-default", which will be added as default client scope to the realms and to all the existing clients (during migration)
- Add 2 protocol mappers to this "oidc-default" client scope:
- OIDCRolesProtocolMapper - the new protocol mapper, which will add roles to the access token instead of adding them automatically as we do now - 
- AudienceClientRolesProtocolMapper - the new protocol mapper, which will add audience to the access token for all the clients, which has any client roles in the token. Need to have lower priority than the OIDCRolesProtocolMapper
- I would still add the "realm-management" client scope, but not add it to any clients. In the docs, we can recommend people to not use "Full Scope Allowed" (which we already do) and use "scope=realm-management" just if they want to call admin REST API with their token.

summary: Run productization and tests against PRs
description:
Prior to merging a PR prod and test should be executed to verify the PR doesn't break anything.
* Bot should initiate the pipelines automatically where the author is a member of the Keycloak organization
* A member of the Keycloak organization should review PR and initate the pipeline with "/test" when the author is not a member of Keycloak organization
* The pipeline should be stable and we should have minimal amount of false negatives
* Prod should include ZIPs and OpenShift images. RPMs to be discussed
* Test should include Keycloak functional tests, CE tests (standalone behave, openshift behave, Arquillian tests) and xPaaS integration tests
* On success the check status on the GitHub PR should be updated to success
* On failure the check status on the GitHub PR should be updated to failed. Logs for both prod and test should be easily available to members of Keycloak organization to debug the issue
* PRs to the pipeline and build config should also be executed prior to merging

summary: External role to role idp mapper update brokered user behavior
description:
This issue is about the behavior of Openid-connect external role to role identity provider mapper.
If the external role is present in external token when importing user, then the role is mapped to this user (in importNewUser).
For later login, the role may be unmapped if the external token does not contain external role anymore (in updateBrokeredUser).
I wonder why the role is not mapped too when already imported user (that was imported without that role) gains that external role.
In my opinion, it make more sense.
I found an old issue that report this behavior, but without any answer (
Is the current behavior wanted, or can it be improved as I propose ? I could submit a patch if so.
The same issue is also for ClaimToRoleMapper

summary: Secure OpenShift 4 with Keycloak
description:
h2. What
Ability to configure Keycloak as the direct IdP for an OpenShift 4 cluster.
h2. Why
OpenShift 4 currently supports using Keycloak as an identity provider, which supports delegating authentication to Keycloak through web based flows. This approach has limitations as OpenShift internal IdP is still the token issuer and authentication directly with the internal IdP is required for non-web based flows.
Integrating directly with Keycloak allows additional use-cases, including:
* Login to CLI via Keycloak
* Clients can obtain tokens from Keycloak to invoke OpenShift endpoints
* Direct management of users within Keycloak only
* Using OAuth proxy to secure applications with Keycloak instead of internal OpenShift IdP
h2. How
There is a previous prototype integrating Keycloak with OpenShift 3 ( This prototype was fully functional and able to replace the internal IdP on OpenShift 3.
OpenShift 4 completely changed how the cluster is configured, which means this approach no longer is valid. Further, Keycloak should be deployed through an Operator rather than through an application template as is done in the previous prototype.
The following work would be needed to fully support the integration with OpenShift 4:
1. Create a new prototype configuring OpenShift 4 in the new way, with an externally started and managed Keycloak instance
2. Use the Keycloak operator to deploy Keycloak to the OpenShift 4 cluster directly, extending the above to support Keycloak deployed within the cluster
3. Add automated testing to the above two use-cases to OpenShift testsuite
4. Document the integration in OpenShift documentation

summary: Support for "defaultLoginOptions" on "init" method in keycloak.js
description:
Method "login" of keycloak.js supports few options to customize login flow. For example things like "scope", "prompt" or "max_age" .

summary: Optimize LogoutEndpoint.logout() to not enumerate all clients when checking redirect URI
description:
Currently the LogoutEndpoint.logout() method (the one used for OIDC frontchannel logout) has quite uneffective way for checking redirect_uri. It calls the method RedirectUtils.verifyRealmRedirectUri, which iterates through all the clients and check if sent redirect_uri matches to any of them.
It will be better if we first lookup UserSessionModel and then check that redirect_uri matches to some of the client attached to UserSessionModel. This will be better for:
- performance as we don't need to iterate through all clients in the realm, but just through those attached to UserSession
- security as we will ensure that sent redirect_uri must match to some URL of any authenticated client applications in the current UserSession. Not any random client in the realm.

summary: Run Javascript adapter tests only once in the testsuite run
description:
During [Jetty adapter test review| we found that Javascript adapter tests will run multiple times in our testsuite (especially when using the [matrix-like approach to the adapter tests| 
Those tests are special, since they don't run on an App Server. They use Javascript on the Auth Server instead. 
There are a couple of ways we can solve this problem:
* Test them only with Undertow
* Create a new, special group for non-App Server, adapter tests
* Test them with some basic App Servers (multiple times), e.g. Wildfly, EAP and Undertow.

summary: Remove org.jboss.metadata module from keycloak adapters
description:
org.jboss.metadata module will be removed from wildfly, so it is necessary to adapt the dependencies of keycloak adapters according to this change.
These are the possible affected files:
{noformat}
git grep org.jboss.metadata | grep module.xml
distribution/adapters/as7-eap6-adapter/as7-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-as7-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/adapters/wf8-adapter/wf8-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-wf8-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/feature-packs/adapter-feature-pack/src/main/resources/modules/system/add-ons/keycloak/org/keycloak/keycloak-wildfly-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/feature-packs/server-feature-pack/src/main/resources/modules/system/layers/keycloak/org/keycloak/keycloak-wildfly-server-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/saml-adapters/as7-eap6-adapter/as7-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-saml-as7-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/saml-adapters/wildfly-adapter/wildfly-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-saml-wildfly-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
{noformat}
From the above list, checking the names looks like that distribution/adapters/wf8-adapter is unnecesary, since it seems it is an adapter for WF8, anyway, it is harmless removing org.jboss.metadata from there and to use the exported dependencies instead.
full_text:

org.jboss.metadata module will be removed from wildfly, so it is necessary to adapt the dependencies of keycloak adapters according to this change.
These are the possible affected files:
{noformat}
git grep org.jboss.metadata | grep module.xml
distribution/adapters/as7-eap6-adapter/as7-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-as7-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/adapters/wf8-adapter/wf8-modules/src/main/resources/modules/org/keycloak/keycloak-wf8-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/feature-packs/adapter-feature-pack/src/main/resources/modules/system/add-ons/keycloak/org/keycloak/keycloak-wildfly-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
distribution/feature-packs/server-feature-pack/src/main/resources/modules/system/layers/keycloak/org/keycloak/keycloak-wildfly-server-subsystem/main/module.xml: <module name="org.jboss.metadata"/>
